per_file.paper_title: Discovery of Van Hove Singularities: Electronic Fingerprints of 3Q Magnetic Order in a van der Waals Quantum Magnet

expected_output.experiment_description: Single crystals of cobalt-intercalated tantalum disulfide, CoxTaS2, are prepared to provide a composition-tunable van der Waals magnetic platform in which Co atoms occupy interlayer sites and form a triangular superlattice coupled to TaS2 conduction layers. For each growth batch, elemental Co, Ta, and S are combined in the nominal molar ratio Co:Ta:S = x:1:2, with x chosen in the range 0.29 to 0.36. The mixture is loaded into alumina crucibles, sealed in quartz tubes under 200 torr partial pressure of Ar, heated to 900 °C, held for 10 days, then furnace-cooled naturally to form a polycrystalline precursor powder. The precursor powder for each batch is ground separately, loaded with iodine transport agent into an evacuated quartz tube, and placed in a horizontal two-zone furnace. The precursor plus iodine are placed in zone 1 and the growth end of the tube in zone 2. Both zones are heated to 850 °C for 6 h for nucleation; then zone 1 is raised to 950 °C while zone 2 remains at 850 °C for 10 days, followed by natural furnace cooling. The goal is to determine whether this chemical-vapor-transport recipe forms macroscopic hexagonal CoxTaS2 crystals over the intended Co-composition interval. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy using an Oxford Instruments Xplore 30 detector is used to determine the Co composition for each crystal by measuring 10 distinct real-space regions per single crystal and reporting the average and standard deviation; the paper does not report the individual region sizes or probe depth.

cxtas2_single_crystal_formation.description: Whether the two-step solid-state precursor and iodine vapor-transport process produced macroscopic CoxTaS2 single crystals.

maximum_reported_crystal_lateral_length_.description: The largest lateral size reported for the collected hexagonal CoxTaS2 crystals.

eds_cobalt_stoichiometry_min_x.description: The minimum Co stoichiometric coefficient among the EDS-characterized CoxTaS2 crystals used for the doping-dependent study.

eds_cobalt_stoichiometry_max_x.description: The maximum Co stoichiometric coefficient among the EDS-characterized CoxTaS2 crystals used for the doping-dependent study.

expected_output.experiment_description: Low-temperature angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy is used to compare the electronic structure of pristine 2H-TaS2 with Co-intercalated Co0.32TaS2, addressing the central question of how Co intercalation modifies TaS2-derived bands and whether additional near-Fermi-level Co-derived electronic states appear. Measurements are performed at Beamline 7.0.2 MAESTRO of the Advanced Light Source using a Scienta Omicron R4000 hemispherical analyzer. The pristine 2H-TaS2 single crystal is a purchased 2D Semiconductors sample; the Co0.32TaS2 sample is grown by the chemical-vapor-transport procedure described in the paper. Data for Co0.32TaS2 are acquired at photon energy hν = 79 eV with linearly horizontal polarization; data for pristine 2H-TaS2 are acquired at hν = 93 eV with linearly horizontal polarization. All spectra are measured at T = 7 K. The momentum-space scope includes Fermi-surface maps spanning the first Brillouin-zone region labeled by Γ0, K0, and M0 for the 1×1 TaS2 lattice and Γ, K, and M for the √3×√3 Co superlattice, plus energy-momentum cuts along M0–Γ0–K0. For Co0.32TaS2, spectra are taken from TaS2-terminated surface regions, with surface terminations differentiated by spatially resolved core-level spectroscopy; the paper does not report the real-space beam spot size or the dimensions of the selected termination domains. Fermi-surface sheets are extracted from the raw momentum maps, and band dispersions are obtained by fitting Lorentzian-shaped momentum-distribution-curve and energy-distribution-curve peak positions. The measurement is configured to quantify band shifts, spin-orbit momentum splitting, and the presence and energy positions of shallow near-EF bands associated with the Co triangular lattice.

expected_output.experiment_description: Polarization-dependent ARPES is performed on TaS2-terminated Co0.32TaS2 to distinguish orbital characters of near-Fermi-level Co-derived bands from TaS2-derived bands, which is central to identifying the electronic fingerprints of the Co triangular magnetic lattice. Measurements are carried out at the Advanced Light Source MAESTRO beamline with hν = 79 eV and a Scienta Omicron R4000 analyzer at T = 7 K. Energy-momentum cuts are acquired along the M0–Γ0–K0 high-symmetry direction using linearly horizontal and linearly vertical photon polarizations. The momentum-space scope covers the Γ0-centered cut through adjacent M0 and K0 points; the selected real-space surface is TaS2-terminated, identified by spatially resolved core-level spectroscopy, but the paper does not report the ARPES spot size or the lateral size of the surface domain. The measurement uses polarization matrix-element contrast, together with orbital-projected calculations, to assign which atomic orbitals dominate the α, β, γK, γM, and ε bands, and to test for any localized nondispersive states in the same energy window.

gamma_band_lv_visibility.description: The visibility of the near-EF γK and γM bands under linearly vertical polarization relative to the linearly horizontal configuration.

epsilon_band_lv_visibility.description: The visibility of the ε band under linearly vertical polarization relative to the linearly horizontal configuration.

localized_nondispersive_band_binding_ene.description: The binding energy of the nondispersive band detected in the linearly vertical polarization spectrum.

gamma_band_dominant_orbital_character.description: The inferred dominant orbital character of the γK and γM near-Fermi-level bands from polarization selection and orbital-projected comparison.

alpha_beta_band_dominant_orbital_charact.description: The inferred dominant orbital character of the highly dispersive α and β bands from polarization selection and orbital-projected comparison.

epsilon_band_dominant_orbital_character.description: The inferred dominant orbital character of the ε band from polarization selection and orbital-projected comparison.

expected_output.experiment_description: Composition-dependent ARPES is used to determine how changing Co content across the reported magnetic boundary near xc ≈ 0.33 affects TaS2-derived bands and Co-derived near-EF bands in CoxTaS2. The central concept is that Co intercalation both dopes the host TaS2-derived bands and creates Co-derived flat bands whose response may be tied to 3Q magnetic order and van Hove singularities. Single crystals with EDS-determined compositions x = 0.29, 0.31, 0.33, 0.34, and 0.36 are measured at T = 7 K at the Advanced Light Source MAESTRO beamline using hν = 79 eV and linearly horizontal polarization. Energy-momentum spectra are acquired along the M0–Γ0–K0 high-symmetry direction on TaS2-terminated regions; the real-space beam size and domain dimensions are not reported. Energy distribution curves at the M point are extracted from the same cuts to determine the α, β, and γM peak positions, while γK band-bottom positions are extracted from EDCs at K. The independent variable is Co stoichiometry x across 0.29–0.36. The measurement is configured to quantify relative band-energy shifts of Ta-derived and Co-derived states while holding the ARPES geometry and low-temperature condition fixed.

alpha_beta_band_downshift_x0_29_to_x0_36.description: The overall energy downshift of the TaS2-derived α and β bands when the Co composition is increased across the measured x interval.

gamma_m_band_upturn_at_x0_36_meV.description: The small upward shift of the γM band extremum at the high-Co end relative to the lower-composition trend.

gamma_k_band_upturn_at_x0_36_meV.description: The small upward shift of the γK band extremum at the high-Co end relative to the lower-composition trend.

co_doping_band_shift_selectivity.description: Which class of bands shows the larger Co-composition-induced energy shift across x = 0.29–0.36.

expected_output.experiment_description: In situ potassium-deposition ARPES is performed on a single Co0.29TaS2 crystal to distinguish intrinsic composition trends from possible sample-to-sample variations and to test the response of the near-EF Co-derived γM band to electron donation at a fixed underlying crystal composition. The central idea is that alkali-metal atoms deposited on the exposed surface donate electrons and tune the chemical potential without changing the bulk Co stoichiometry or magnetic-ion arrangement. A TaS2-terminated Co0.29TaS2 surface is measured at T = 7 K at the Advanced Light Source MAESTRO beamline using hν = 79 eV; spectra are collected along Γ0–K0 before potassium deposition and after successive deposition rounds labeled first through fifth. The paper does not report deposition rate, deposition time, K coverage, real-space beam spot size, or the lateral size of the probed surface region. EDCs at the M point are used to track α, β, and γM peak positions after each deposition step. The independent variable is potassium deposition number, with the same sample and ARPES geometry retained across the series.

alpha_beta_downshift_after_four_k_deposi.description: The approximate downshift of the TaS2-derived α and β bands after four potassium deposition rounds, benchmarked against the composition-induced shift over x = 0.29–0.36.

gamma_m_response_to_k_deposition.description: The measured response of the Co-derived γM peak position to successive potassium deposition within the reported experimental resolution.

expected_output.experiment_description: Doping-dependent Fermi-surface ARPES maps of CoxTaS2 are acquired to test for momentum-space fingerprints of the transition between the low-doping 3Q magnetic regime and the higher-doping helical regime. The central mechanism being probed is that a Co triangular-lattice band near three-quarters filling can host van Hove singularities, and 3Q magnetic order modifies the Fermi-surface topology and redistributes spectral weight between the tips of γ pockets and the M point. Single crystals with Co compositions spanning x = 0.29 to 0.36 are measured at T = 7 K with hν = 79 eV on TaS2-terminated surfaces at the Advanced Light Source. The momentum-space scope includes Fermi-surface intensity maps around the Co-superlattice Brillouin zone, including K and M points, with representative maps for x = 0.29, 0.32, and 0.34 and extracted γ-pocket contours for the full composition series. Momentum-distribution curves along the K–M direction are compared for x = 0.29 and x = 0.36. The spectral-weight metric is defined as the ARPES Fermi-surface intensity at the tip of the γ pocket divided by the intensity at the M point, using the same Fermi-surface mapping convention. The paper does not report the real-space beam spot size, scan area, or number of repeated cleaves for each composition.

gamma_pocket_size_trend_with_cobalt_comp.description: The trend of the extracted γ Fermi-pocket size as Co composition is increased across the measured series.

tip_to_m_spectral_weight_ratio_x0_29.description: The ARPES Fermi-surface spectral-weight ratio between the γ-pocket tip and M point for the x = 0.29 sample, read from the plotted ratio.

tip_to_m_spectral_weight_ratio_x0_36.description: The ARPES Fermi-surface spectral-weight ratio between the γ-pocket tip and M point for the x = 0.36 sample, read from the plotted ratio.

expected_output.experiment_description: ARPES band-dispersion cuts along the Co-superlattice K–M–K′ direction are measured as a function of Co composition to directly test the central proposed electronic fingerprint of 3Q magnetic order: reconstruction of the near-EF Co-derived band into an inverse-Mexican-hat-like dispersion with van-Hove-related band extrema displaced away from M. CoxTaS2 single crystals with x = 0.29, 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, and 0.36 are measured at T = 7 K using hν = 79 eV at the Advanced Light Source on TaS2-terminated surfaces. The momentum-space scope is a one-dimensional cut through K–M–K′ of the Co-superlattice Brillouin zone; second-derivative images with respect to energy are derived from the raw spectra, and EDC stacks are analyzed at selected momenta including the γ-band Fermi momentum kF and the M point. The spectral-weight metric is defined as the ratio of the EDC peak intensity at kF to the EDC peak intensity at M along the same cut. Band dispersions for x = 0.29 and x = 0.36 are extracted from EDC peak positions; the dot size in the plotted extraction encodes relative EDC peak intensity. The real-space beam spot size, lateral homogeneity length, and number of repeated sample locations are not reported. The independent variable is Co composition x, and the measurement targets the low-energy Co-derived band curvature and spectral-weight transfer across the reported magnetic-regime boundary near xc ≈ 0.33.

per_file.paper_title: Device-independent quantum memory certification in two-point measurement experiments

expected_output.experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement certification of a local qubit quantum memory is implemented on a trapped-ion processor to test whether temporal correlations can rule out a classical, entanglement-breaking memory model without trusting device internals. The processor consists of a linear chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions in a macroscopic linear Paul trap; the two outer ions encode qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion is a spacer to reduce optical addressing cross-talk over the ion-chain length. Qubit manipulation uses an individually addressed 729 nm laser with linewidth below 1 Hz incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis through a crossed-AOD addressing system; state readout uses resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected on an EMCCD camera, with fluorescence corresponding to population in the S1/2 manifold and absence of fluorescence to population in the D5/2 manifold. The sequence prepares the two outer ions A′+E in a Bell state using a Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit E is spectroscopically shelved into unused D5/2 levels during the mid-circuit measurement on A′ to reduce measurement back-action. The first measurement setting X is sampled from four Pauli choices {σx, σz, −σx, −σz}, with binary outcome A. A measure-and-prepare instrument is implemented so that the post-measurement qubit A is prepared in a σx eigenstate depending only on A and not on X; in the memory-test assignment, outcome A=1 corresponds to |+⟩ and A=0 corresponds to |−⟩, with equivalent sign conventions handled by post-processing of the four X settings. After readout, Doppler and polarization-gradient recooling are applied because the fluorescence measurement heats the shared motional mode; resolved sideband recooling is not used after the mid-circuit measurement in order not to disturb E. With no deliberately added storage-delay sweep in this certification run, qubits A+E undergo a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP, where the CNOT is composed of one Mølmer-Sørensen interaction and local rotations R^C_0(π/2), R^T_π(π/2), R^T_{π/4}(π), MS^C,T_XX(π/2), and R^T_{π/2}(π/2). The second-time qubit B is measured in the (σx+σz)/√2 basis. Repeated runs over the four X settings produce the empirical probabilities Pr(A,B|X). The device-independent memory witness is Γ = Σ_{b0,b1} inf_{x∈{0,1,2,3}} Σ_{a∈{0,1}} Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x), whose classical instrumental bound is Γ≥1. The reported qubit-memory quality is the Uhlmann fidelity FMemory between the Choi-Jamiołkowski state of the implemented memory channel and that of an ideal identity memory, lower-bounded from Γ using FMemory ≥ 1/2[1 − (Γ − 2 + S_K)/(√2 − S_K)], with S_K=(8+7√2)/17. To assess cross-talk in the same spatially local ion-chain geometry, the Pearl parameter Δ = max_a Σ_b sup_x Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x) is computed, and the average causal direct effect is defined as ACDE = sup |Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) − Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b)| over the indicated binary outcomes and settings; in this implementation the same empirical probability table and post-processed intervention assignments are used to estimate these quantities.

instrumental_inequality_gamma.description: The measured value of the device-independent two-point-measurement memory witness Γ computed from Pr(A,B|X).

memory_fidelity_lower_bound_fraction.description: The device-independent lower bound on the fidelity of the implemented qubit memory channel to an ideal identity memory channel.

classical_memory_model_excluded.description: Whether the measured temporal correlations exclude the classical instrumental-memory bound for the tested qubit memory configuration.

pearl_cross_talk_parameter_delta.description: The measured Pearl-inequality parameter Δ used as an observational witness for possible cross-talk influences from X to B not mediated by A.

average_causal_direct_effect.description: The measured average causal direct effect quantifying direct cross-talk influence from the first measurement setting X to the later outcome B under interventions fixing A.

expected_output.experiment_description: Temporal classicalisation of the same device-independent two-point-measurement qubit-memory protocol is characterized by sweeping a storage waiting time between the mid-circuit measurement-and-repreparation step and the CNOT-plus-virtual-SWAP readout operation. The physical platform, spatial geometry, optical addressing, shelving of the E ion, 397 nm EMCCD fluorescence readout, recooling after the first measurement, first measurement settings X∈{σx, σz, −σx, −σz}, σx-eigenstate post-measurement preparation of qubit A, and final B measurement in the (σx+σz)/√2 basis are the same as in the no-delay certification sequence. The added waiting time is swept from 0 ms to 100 ms. During this interval, dynamical decoupling echo pulses are inserted every 2.5 ms to suppress quasi-static and 100 Hz magnetic-field noise, while active magnetic-field compensation suppresses the 50 Hz mains component. For every waiting time, repeated experimental shots over all four X settings provide Pr(A,B|X), from which the rescaled violation of the classicality inequality is computed; positive rescaled values correspond to a violation of the classical temporal-causal bound, and the certification duration is determined from the waiting-time range over which the data still certify a non-classical qubit memory under the stated protocol.

certified_quantum_memory_duration_ms.description: The storage duration for which the two-point-measurement protocol certifies the trapped-ion qubit memory as non-classical.

expected_output.experiment_description: A two-point-measurement experiment is performed on the same three-ion 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor to test non-classical causal relations by coherently varying the balance between common-cause and direct-cause mechanisms. The two outer ions encode A′ and E and the middle ion is a spacer; qubit control uses the 729 nm addressed laser at 67.5 degrees, and readout uses 397 nm fluorescence imaging on an EMCCD. The outer ions are initially prepared in a Bell state by a Mølmer-Sørensen gate. The first measurement on A′ uses the same four sampled Pauli settings X∈{σx, σz, −σx, −σz} with binary outcome A, while E is shelved during the mid-circuit measurement and the ion chain is recooled afterward. In this causal-relation protocol, the measure-and-prepare state of A is a σy eigenstate depending only on A: |+i⟩ for A=0 and |−i⟩ for A=1, with sign conventions handled by the four-setting post-processing table. The two-qubit operation after the first measurement is the partial-swap gate U_PS(α)=cos(α/2) id + i sin(α/2) U_swap, implemented as MS_ZZ(−α/2)·MS_YY(−α/2)·MS_XX(−α/2), where the rotation angle is controlled by laser intensity while keeping the gate time fixed. The independent control parameter α is swept over the interval 0 to π radians. The final measurement of B is σx. For each α, repeated runs over all X settings yield Pr(A,B|X), from which the same classical causal inequality witness is evaluated to determine whether the observed process can be simulated as a classical mixture of common-cause and direct-cause processes.

nonclassical_causal_relations_certified.description: Whether the partial-swap two-point-measurement data certify causal relations outside classical common-cause/direct-cause mixtures for some swept gate angles.

alpha_interval_with_reported_classical_i.description: The reported swept partial-swap angle interval in which the measured causal witness violates the classical causal bound.

expected_output.experiment_description: The effective coherence time relevant to the trapped-ion quantum-memory decay model is characterized independently with Ramsey-type measurements on the same 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor. The qubit is manipulated with the addressed 729 nm laser and read out by 397 nm fluorescence imaging, while the magnetic environment is treated as in the memory-decay experiment: active compensation suppresses coherent 50 Hz mains magnetic-field noise, and a dynamical-decoupling echo sequence with pulses separated by 2.5 ms suppresses quasi-static and 100 Hz components. Ramsey experiments are run over a waiting-time sweep spanning 0 ms to 200 ms, and the Ramsey contrast is fit with an exponential decay model corresponding to Lorentzian-distributed frequency noise. The fitted decay constant is used as the effective T2 coherence time of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling conditions used for the quantum-memory certification sequence.

effective_coherence_time_T2_ms.description: The exponential Ramsey-contrast decay time of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling conditions used in the memory experiment.

per_file.paper_title: Voltage-controlled topological spin textures in the monolayer limit

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: quantify the hBN dielectric response used to convert applied voltage in the monolayer CrI3 vertical device into out-of-plane electric field and electrostatic doping, which are the control knobs for voltage-tunable DMI and magnetic anisotropy. The hBN dielectric layer is part of a graphene–hBN–CrI3–graphene/graphite device stack on SiO2/Si. Its thickness is determined by optical contrast on an hBN–SiO2–Si structure: white light is normally incident and focused with a 50×, NA = 0.45 microscope objective, reflected light is collected through a beamsplitter into a spectrometer, and a CCD records the spectrally resolved reflected signal. The optical contrast is defined as C = (R_SiO2 − R_SiO2+hBN)/R_SiO2, where R_SiO2 is the normal-incidence reflection coefficient of bare SiO2/Si and R_SiO2+hBN is the coefficient for hBN-covered SiO2/Si. The relative dielectric constant of the hBN dielectric is measured using a ferroelectric analyzer; electrode geometry, AC amplitude, and frequency are not specified in the provided text. The spatial scope is the dielectric flake used in the gated device; the exact mapped area and number of measurement points are not reported.

hbn_relative_dielectric_constant.description: The measured relative dielectric constant of the hBN dielectric layer used in the gated monolayer CrI3 device.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: verify that the active CrI3 flake in the voltage-controlled topological-spin-texture device is in the monolayer magnetic limit by probing spin-lattice-coupled Raman modes. Polarization-resolved and temperature-dependent Raman measurements are performed on the active CrI3 region of the hBN-encapsulated/gated device using a Witec Alpha 300R Plus low-wavenumber confocal Raman microscope integrated with a closed-cycle He optical cryostat and superconducting magnet. Excitation is a 633 nm laser with approximately 0.3 mW power. A 50× objective with NA = 0.45 is used at cryogenic temperature and under magnetic-field-compatible conditions. Raman signals are collected through a photonic crystal fiber into a spectrometer with an 1800 g/mm grating. Cross-polarized (XY) and co-linear (XX) configurations are obtained by rotating an analyzer before the fiber. Typical integration time is 120 s. Temperature is swept across the low-temperature ferromagnetic regime and above the magnetic ordering range while monitoring the same confocal spot or designated active region; the exact lateral spot size, active-area dimensions, and number of independent positions are not reported. The measurement targets the Raman-active phonon selection and its temperature-dependent coupling to magnetic order in monolayer CrI3.

a1g_raman_phonon_frequency_cm_minus1.description: The measured Raman shift of the A1g phonon mode used for monolayer CrI3 identification.

raman_spin_lattice_coupling_onset_temper.description: The temperature scale at which the polarization-resolved Raman response changes due to spin-lattice coupling in the CrI3 monolayer.

a1g_raman_polarization_channels.description: The polarization channels in which the A1g Raman phonon is detected for the monolayer CrI3 device.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: establish the baseline magnetic state of the target monolayer CrI3 device before applying voltage-induced DMI/anisotropy control, so that later anomalous circular-dichroism features can be assigned to voltage-created topological spin textures rather than ordinary ferromagnetic hysteresis. Polar reflective magnetic circular dichroism (RMCD) is measured on a designated region of the monolayer CrI3 device using a magneto-optical-electric joint-measurement scanning imaging system based on a Witec Alpha 300R Plus confocal platform, a closed-cycle superconducting magnet with up to 7 T field capability, and a cryogen-free optical cryostat with 10 K base temperature. A 633 nm laser with fixed power about 3 µW is modulated by a photoelastic modulator at 50 kHz, reflected from a non-polarizing beamsplitter with R/T = 30/70, and focused onto the active CrI3 region using a 50× objective with NA = 0.55. The reflected beam is collected by the same objective and detected by a photomultiplier tube coupled to a lock-in amplifier. The device gate voltage is fixed at 0 V. Out-of-plane magnetic field µ0H is swept in both directions through the low-field switching region, and high-field RMCD response is also checked to test for interlayer antiferromagnetic signatures. Temperature-dependent RMCD is acquired on the same device region to determine the magnetic ordering temperature. The confocal spot is positioned within the active region; the exact illuminated area, distance from edges, and number of spatial positions are not reported.

zero_gate_coercive_field_T.description: The coercive out-of-plane magnetic field of the monolayer CrI3 device measured by RMCD at zero gate voltage.

zero_gate_curie_temperature_K.description: The Curie temperature of the monolayer CrI3 device measured by temperature-dependent RMCD at zero gate voltage.

high_field_rmcd_step_present_zero_gate.description: Whether the zero-gate RMCD loop contains a high-field step associated with interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: test voltage creation and continuous manipulation of topological spin textures in the strict monolayer CrI3 limit by using reflective topological circular dichroism, an optical-frequency analogue of the topological Hall effect. The same air-isolated gated monolayer CrI3/hBN/graphene device is measured at 10 K with the polar RMCD setup: 633 nm laser, approximately 3 µW power, 50 kHz photoelastic modulation, non-polarizing R/T = 30/70 beamsplitter, 50× NA = 0.55 objective, photomultiplier detection, lock-in readout, superconducting out-of-plane magnetic field, and a voltage source meter connected to the vertical electrodes. Gate voltage Vg is swept over the positive electron-doping range from 0 V to about 16 V, with representative loops at 0, 8, 12, and 16 V and phase maps over approximately 0–15/16 V. Out-of-plane magnetic field µ0H is swept over the switching/topological range in both directions, approximately within ±0.2 T in the plotted maps. The total RMCD signal is decomposed as I_RMCD = I_RCD(M) + I_RCD(T), where I_RCD(M) is the conventional reflective circular dichroism component proportional to the out-of-plane ferromagnetic magnetization background and I_RCD(T) is the topological circular dichroism component proportional to topological charge density; I_RCD(T) is obtained by subtracting the conventional magnetic background from total RMCD. RCDT peak positions are extracted by Gaussian fitting and plotted versus gate voltage. The measurement is made on a designated confocal spot/active region of the device; exact lateral spot diameter, spatial map area, and number of independent devices or positions are not reported. The phase-mapping objective is to determine the voltage range in which nontrivial topological magnetic order is optically detected and how its characteristic field shifts with voltage as magnetic anisotropy evolves from perpendicular toward in-plane.

topological_circular_dichroism_onset_vol.description: The gate voltage at which the RCDT signal first emerges from the near-zero background in the voltage-dependent RMCD phase diagram.

type_i_to_type_ii_skyrmion_transition_vo.description: The gate voltage at which the voltage-dependent RCDT response changes between the low-voltage topological regime associated with perpendicular anisotropy and the high-voltage regime associated with small in-plane anisotropy.

positive_topological_charge_peak_field_s.description: The fitted slope of the magnetic-field position of the RCDT peak associated with positive topological charge as a function of gate voltage in the linear voltage-tuning regime.

negative_topological_charge_peak_field_s.description: The fitted slope of the magnetic-field position of the RCDT peak associated with negative topological charge as a function of gate voltage in the linear voltage-tuning regime.

conventional_rcdm_hysteresis_present_at_.description: Whether a residual conventional ferromagnetic RCDM hysteresis component remains in the RMCD loop under the high positive gate-voltage condition.

voltage_induced_topological_phase_sequen.description: The sequence of magnetic phases inferred from voltage-dependent RMCD/RCDT under the positive-gate sweep.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: characterize the thermal stability and field-temperature phase boundaries of voltage-induced two-dimensional topological spin textures in monolayer CrI3 under a gate condition that drives the system into the high-voltage, small-in-plane-anisotropy regime. The gated monolayer CrI3 device is biased at +16 V and measured by polar RMCD/RCDT using the same optical configuration: 633 nm laser, about 3 µW power, 50 kHz PEM modulation, 50× NA = 0.55 objective, PMT and lock-in detection, closed-cycle cryostat, and superconducting out-of-plane magnetic field. RMCD loops are collected at discrete temperatures including 10, 15, 18, 21, 24, and 27 K, and field-temperature maps are acquired over roughly 10–27 K while sweeping µ0H in both directions across approximately ±0.2 T. Positive-to-negative and negative-to-positive field-sweep directions are recorded separately to distinguish opposite topological-charge signs. RMCD peak positions and half-peak widths are obtained by Gaussian fitting; peak positions are plotted versus temperature. report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept: quantify the hBN dielectric response used to convert applied voltage in the monolayer CrI3 vertical device into out-of-plane electric field and electrostatic doping, which are the control knobs for voltage-tunable DMI and magnetic anisotropy. The hBN dielectric layer is part of a graphene–hBN–CrI3–graphene/graphite device stack on SiO2/Si. Its thickness is determined by optical contrast on an hBN–SiO2–Si structure: white light is normally incident and focused with a 50×, NA = 0.45 microscope objective, reflected light is collected through a beamsplitter into a spectrometer, and a CCD records the spectrally resolved reflected signal. The optical contrast is defined as C = (R_SiO2 − R_SiO2+hBN)/R_SiO2, where R_SiO2 is the normal-incidence reflection coefficient of bare SiO2/Si and R_SiO2+hBN is the coefficient for hBN-covered SiO2/Si. The relative dielectric constant of the hBN dielectric is measured using a ferroelectric analyzer; electrode geometry, AC amplitude, and frequency are not specified in the provided text. The spatial scope is the dielectric flake used in the gated device; the exact mapped area and number of measurement points are not reported.

result_rows.description: The measured relative dielectric constant of the hBN dielectric layer used in the gated monolayer CrI3 device.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept: verify that the active CrI3 flake in the voltage-controlled topological-spin-texture device is in the monolayer magnetic limit by probing spin-lattice-coupled Raman modes. Polarization-resolved and temperature-dependent Raman measurements are performed on the active CrI3 region of the hBN-encapsulated/gated device using a Witec Alpha 300R Plus low-wavenumber confocal Raman microscope integrated with a closed-cycle He optical cryostat and superconducting magnet. Excitation is a 633 nm laser with approximately 0.3 mW power. A 50× objective with NA = 0.45 is used at cryogenic temperature and under magnetic-field-compatible conditions. Raman signals are collected through a photonic crystal fiber into a spectrometer with an 1800 g/mm grating. Cross-polarized (XY) and co-linear (XX) configurations are obtained by rotating an analyzer before the fiber. Typical integration time is 120 s. Temperature is swept across the low-temperature ferromagnetic regime and above the magnetic ordering range while monitoring the same confocal spot or designated active region; the exact lateral spot size, active-area dimensions, and number of independent positions are not reported. The measurement targets the Raman-active phonon selection and its temperature-dependent coupling to magnetic order in monolayer CrI3.

result_rows.description: The measured Raman shift of the A1g phonon mode used for monolayer CrI3 identification.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept: establish the baseline magnetic state of the target monolayer CrI3 device before applying voltage-induced DMI/anisotropy control, so that later anomalous circular-dichroism features can be assigned to voltage-created topological spin textures rather than ordinary ferromagnetic hysteresis. Polar reflective magnetic circular dichroism (RMCD) is measured on a designated region of the monolayer CrI3 device using a magneto-optical-electric joint-measurement scanning imaging system based on a Witec Alpha 300R Plus confocal platform, a closed-cycle superconducting magnet with up to 7 T field capability, and a cryogen-free optical cryostat with 10 K base temperature. A 633 nm laser with fixed power about 3 µW is modulated by a photoelastic modulator at 50 kHz, reflected from a non-polarizing beamsplitter with R/T = 30/70, and focused onto the active CrI3 region using a 50× objective with NA = 0.55. The reflected beam is collected by the same objective and detected by a photomultiplier tube coupled to a lock-in amplifier. The device gate voltage is fixed at 0 V. Out-of-plane magnetic field µ0H is swept in both directions through the low-field switching region, and high-field RMCD response is also checked to test for interlayer antiferromagnetic signatures. Temperature-dependent RMCD is acquired on the same device region to determine the magnetic ordering temperature. The confocal spot is positioned within the active region; the exact illuminated area, distance from edges, and number of spatial positions are not reported.

result_rows.description: The coercive out-of-plane magnetic field of the monolayer CrI3 device measured by RMCD at zero gate voltage.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept: test voltage creation and continuous manipulation of topological spin textures in the strict monolayer CrI3 limit by using reflective topological circular dichroism, an optical-frequency analogue of the topological Hall effect. The same air-isolated gated monolayer CrI3/hBN/graphene device is measured at 10 K with the polar RMCD setup: 633 nm laser, approximately 3 µW power, 50 kHz photoelastic modulation, non-polarizing R/T = 30/70 beamsplitter, 50× NA = 0.55 objective, photomultiplier detection, lock-in readout, superconducting out-of-plane magnetic field, and a voltage source meter connected to the vertical electrodes. Gate voltage Vg is swept over the positive electron-doping range from 0 V to about 16 V, with representative loops at 0, 8, 12, and 16 V and phase maps over approximately 0–15/16 V. Out-of-plane magnetic field µ0H is swept over the switching/topological range in both directions, approximately within ±0.2 T in the plotted maps. The total RMCD signal is decomposed as I_RMCD = I_RCD(M) + I_RCD(T), where I_RCD(M) is the conventional reflective circular dichroism component proportional to the out-of-plane ferromagnetic magnetization background and I_RCD(T) is the topological circular dichroism component proportional to topological charge density; I_RCD(T) is obtained by subtracting the conventional magnetic background from total RMCD. RCDT peak positions are extracted by Gaussian fitting and plotted versus gate voltage. The measurement is made on a designated confocal spot/active region of the device; exact lateral spot diameter, spatial map area, and number of independent devices or positions are not reported. The phase-mapping objective is to determine the voltage range in which nontrivial topological magnetic order is optically detected and how its characteristic field shifts with voltage as magnetic anisotropy evolves from perpendicular toward in-plane.

per_file.paper_title: Fundamental Tests of Quantum Geometric Bounds in Ionic and Covalent Insulators using Inelastic X-Ray Scattering

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: inelastic x-ray scattering (IXS) is used as a direct density-response probe from which the quantum Fisher information density f_Q, Bures metric g_q, and longitudinal quantum weight K(q) of insulating solids can be obtained, enabling comparison of quantum-information delocalization in covalently bonded diamond and ionically bonded LiF. The experiment uses room-temperature IXS at Sector 9-ID of the Advanced Photon Source. A liquid-nitrogen-cooled Si(111) primary monochromator and Si(333) secondary channel-cut prepare the incident beam. For diamond, spectra are collected at incident photon energy 8981.8 eV using a Ge(733) backscattering analyzer with 0.3 eV energy resolution and momentum transfer q parallel to crystallographic direction (1,-1,0). For LiF, spectra are collected at incident photon energy 6482.5 eV using a Ge(531) analyzer with 140 meV energy resolution and q parallel to (1,0,0). The nominal momentum resolution is about 0.15 Å^-1. Energy-loss scans are obtained by scanning the incident energy over electronic excitations up to 100 eV; the plotted momentum-transfer sequence spans approximately q = 0.32 to 4.55 Å^-1. The quasi-elastic contribution below about 3 eV is removed, and the remaining spectra are treated as the dynamic structure factor/density response for electronic excitations above the band gaps. The spatial sampling area, beam footprint, number of probed sample positions, and sample mosaic/defect mapping are not specified in the text; the geometric scope explicitly reported is the reciprocal-space direction and momentum-resolution window. The spectra are converted to χ''(q,ω) in physical units by enforcing the f-sum rule after extrapolating intensity above the 100 eV cutoff as I(q,ℏω>Ω)=c(q)Ω^3/(ℏω)^3, where Ω=100 eV and c(q) is the average spectral intensity from 94 to 100 eV at fixed q. The partial f-sum normalization uses eight active electrons per primitive diamond unit cell with primitive lattice constant 2.52 Å and ten active electrons per LiF primitive unit cell with primitive lattice constant 2.84 Å. The analysis computes g_q=-(ℏ/π)∫_0^∞dω tanh(βω/2)χ''(q,ω) and f_Q=4g_q at room temperature, with β the inverse thermal energy; for the high-energy electronic spectrum the Bose factor is effectively unity.

lif_small_q_qfi_power_law_exponent.description: The approximate exponent of the small-momentum power-law decrease of the quantum Fisher information density in LiF as a function of q.

diamond_qfi_relative_to_lif_over_measure.description: The material ordering of the quantum Fisher information density when comparing diamond and LiF over the common measured momentum-transfer range.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: the same IXS-derived density response can be Kramers-Kronig transformed to obtain the static electronic longitudinal dielectric response needed to test quantum-geometric electrostatic bounds. The experiment uses the room-temperature IXS spectra of diamond and LiF described for the quantum-Fisher-information measurement, with elastic scattering removed and spectra scaled by the f-sum rule using the finite 100 eV electronic window and the ω^-3 high-energy extrapolation. The real part χ'(q,ω) is computed from χ''(q,ω) using the Kramers-Kronig relation χ'(q,ω)=(2/π)P∫_0^∞ dω' [ω'χ''(q,ω')/(ω'^2-ω^2)], where P denotes the principal value. The static electronic dielectric function is then obtained from ε(q,ω)^-1 = 1 + V(q)χ(q,ω), with V(q)=4πe^2/q^2, evaluated at a small nonzero energy inside the electronic gap; the figure caption specifies extraction below the gap at 4.5 eV. Momentum transfers are along (1,-1,0) for diamond and (1,0,0) for LiF, with momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1. The high-q spatial-frequency regime is analyzed by fitting the extracted ε(q) for q approximately greater than 2.5 Å^-1 to the short-wavelength screening form ε(q)=1+exp(-αq), where q is in Å^-1 and α is the fitted real-space decay length in Å associated with atomic-scale electronic polarization. The beam footprint, number of real-space locations, and independent sample count are not specified; homogeneity is assessed only through the reciprocal-space q-dependent dielectric response extracted from the spectra.

diamond_dielectric_high_q_decay_length_A.description: The fitted decay length α of the high-momentum electronic dielectric response of diamond using ε(q)=1+exp(-αq).

lif_dielectric_high_q_decay_length_A.description: The fitted decay length α of the high-momentum electronic dielectric response of LiF using ε(q)=1+exp(-αq).

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: the IXS-derived Bures metric is converted into the dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q), a reciprocal-space measure of electronic localization and quantum-information sharing in insulating bonds, to compare a covalent insulator, diamond, against an ionic insulator, LiF. The analysis uses the same room-temperature IXS density-response spectra, elastic-line removal, f-sum normalization, ω^-3 extrapolation above 100 eV, and q directions as in the QFI measurement: diamond at 8981.8 eV with Ge(733) analyzer, 0.3 eV energy resolution, q parallel to (1,-1,0); LiF at 6482.5 eV with Ge(531) analyzer, 140 meV energy resolution, q parallel to (1,0,0); momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1. The measured q range used for the quantum-weight plot is the finite-q electronic-response range shown in the paper, approximately q≈1.5–4.6 Å^-1 for diamond and q≈1.3–3.8 Å^-1 for LiF. The quantity compared is aK(q)=-(πa/2q^2)f_Q, equivalently proportional to a g_q/q^2, where a is the primitive lattice constant, q is the magnitude of the momentum transfer, f_Q is the quantum Fisher information density, and g_q is the Bures metric obtained from χ''(q,ω). The interpretation is that aK(q) below or above unity in the small-q limit distinguishes charge fluctuations largely confined within one primitive unit cell from fluctuations extending over multiple primitive unit cells. The real-space beam footprint, scan area, number of sample locations, and defect/edge exclusion criteria are not specified; the reported homogeneity context is the reproducibility of the q-dependent reciprocal-space trend after applying the stated spectral normalization and elastic removal.

diamond_small_q_dimensionless_quantum_we.description: The inferred small-momentum category of the dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) for diamond relative to unity.

lif_small_q_dimensionless_quantum_weight.description: The inferred small-momentum category of the dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) for LiF relative to unity.

small_q_dimensionless_quantum_weight_mat.description: The inferred material ordering of the small-momentum dimensionless quantum weight aK(q).

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: the experimentally extracted dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) is tested against wavevector-dependent electrostatic bounds that constrain the possible quantum geometry of density fluctuations in an insulator. The test uses room-temperature IXS spectra of diamond and LiF scaled by the f-sum rule, extrapolated above Ω=100 eV as ω^-3, converted to χ''(q,ω), integrated to obtain f_Q and g_q, and combined with ε(q) extracted from the Kramers-Kronig procedure. Diamond is measured with q parallel to (1,-1,0), incident energy 8981.8 eV, Ge(733) analyzer, and 0.3 eV energy resolution; LiF is measured with q parallel to (1,0,0), incident energy 6482.5 eV, Ge(531) analyzer, and 140 meV energy resolution; both use momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1 and room-temperature electronic energy-loss scans up to 100 eV. The bounds evaluated are (1-ε(q)^-1)E_g ≤ 4e^2K(q) ≤ sqrt(1-ε(q)^-1)ℏω_p, with the dimensionless plotted quantity multiplied by the primitive lattice constant a. Here ε(q) is the electronic static longitudinal dielectric function extracted from IXS, E_g is the smallest electronic excitation gap used for the material, ω_p=sqrt(4πne^2/m) is the plasma frequency defined using the effective electron density n from the partial f-sum rule, e is the elementary charge, m is the bare electron mass, and K(q) is the longitudinal quantum weight derived from the Bures metric. The q-dependent comparison is made over the same finite momentum ranges as the aK(q) extraction. The spatial/geometric scope is reciprocal-space only; beam footprint, real-space scan area, and number of independently measured sample positions are not specified.

diamond_quantum_weight_within_q_dependen.description: Whether the measured finite-q dimensionless quantum weight values for diamond satisfy the experimentally evaluated q-dependent electrostatic bounds.

lif_quantum_weight_within_q_dependent_el.description: Whether the measured finite-q dimensionless quantum weight values for LiF satisfy the experimentally evaluated q-dependent electrostatic bounds.

diamond_zero_q_bound_position_category.description: The qualitative position approached by the inferred small-q diamond quantum weight within the zero-wavevector electrostatic bound interval.

lif_zero_q_bound_position_category.description: The qualitative position approached by the inferred small-q LiF quantum weight within the zero-wavevector electrostatic bound interval.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept: the experimentally extracted dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) is tested against wavevector-dependent electrostatic bounds that constrain the possible quantum geometry of density fluctuations in an insulator. Diamond is measured with q parallel to (1,-1,0), incident energy 8981.8 eV, Ge(733) analyzer, and 0.3 eV energy resolution; LiF is measured with q parallel to (1,0,0), incident energy 6482.5 eV, Ge(531) analyzer, and 140 meV energy resolution; both use momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1 and room-temperature electronic energy-loss scans up to 100 eV. The bounds evaluated are (1-ε(q)^-1)E_g ≤ 4e^2K(q) ≤ sqrt(1-ε(q)^-1)ℏω_p, with the dimensionless plotted quantity multiplied by the primitive lattice constant a. Here ε(q) is the electronic static longitudinal dielectric function extracted from IXS, E_g is the smallest electronic excitation gap used for the material, ω_p=sqrt(4πne^2/m) is the plasma frequency defined using the effective electron density n from the partial f-sum rule, e is the elementary charge, m is the bare electron mass, and K(q) is the longitudinal quantum weight derived from the Bures metric. The q-dependent comparison is made over the same finite momentum ranges as the aK(q) extraction. per_file.paper_title: First Experimental Demonstration of Beam Storage by Three-Dimensional Spiral Injection Scheme for Ultra-Compact Storage Rings

expected_output.experiment_description: A proof-of-principle ultra-compact weak-focusing electron storage ring is operated to test the central concept of three-dimensional spiral injection: an injected beam enters a solenoid-type storage magnet with a vertical pitch angle so that the solenoidal fringe field and a weak-focusing radial field guide the orbit in three dimensions, while a comparatively long pulsed kicker supplies small vertical kicks over many turns rather than requiring a single-turn nanosecond kicker. The electron beam is generated by a thermionic electron gun and chopper system with momentum p = 297 keV/c, kinetic energy 80 keV, and injected bunch width 100 ns. The transport line consists of three rotatable quadrupole magnets, one bending magnet, and a pair of steering magnets; it injects the beam into a 22 cm storage ring inside a storage magnet at a pitch angle of 0.7 rad relative to the horizontal X-Y plane. The storage magnet consists of main and auxiliary solenoidal coils operated with opposite polarities to keep the solenoidal field on the storage midplane Z = 0 cm at Bz = 8.77 mT while producing a weak-focusing field potential with field index of order 10^-2 in the storage region. A kicker coil system with inductance 1.3 microhenry is located at Z = ±15 cm and is driven, for the kicker-on condition, with a 45 A, 140 ns pulsed current to generate a radial field component configured to maintain downward steering during spiral injection. The beam revolution period in the compact ring is 4.7 ns. Beam storage is diagnosed destructively with a plastic scintillating-fiber probe inserted vertically from above into the storage region; the fiber is 1 mm in diameter and 20 cm long, read by a photomultiplier tube, and has an electron CSDA range of about 100 micrometre for 297 keV/c electrons in the scintillator material. For the representative storage test, the probe tip is positioned at the storage midplane so that the fiber covers Z = 0 cm to Z = 20 cm within the storage region. The SciFi-probe voltage waveform, a bottom plastic-scintillator beam-loss monitor waveform, and the kicker current waveform measured by a Rogowski coil are recorded for kicker-on and kicker-off conditions, with each waveform averaged over 1000 injected shots. The operational storage criterion is defined as a SciFi-probe signal exceeding 5 times sigma_noise for a duration of at least 1 microsecond, where sigma_noise is the rms fluctuation of the voltage in a pre-injection time window; this threshold corresponds to a time much longer than the injected pulse width and to many revolutions, and is intended to distinguish stored beam from transiently circulating or lost particles.

beam_storage_observed_with_kicker.description: Whether the SciFi-probe waveform satisfies the predefined storage criterion under the spiral-injection condition with the pulsed kicker activated.

beam_storage_observed_without_kicker.description: Whether the SciFi-probe waveform satisfies the predefined storage criterion under otherwise comparable injection conditions without the pulsed kicker.

stored_signal_persistence_lower_bound_us.description: Lower bound on the duration for which the SciFi-probe storage signal remains above the predefined noise threshold in the kicker-on condition.

transient_signal_duration_without_kicker.description: Approximate duration scale of the SciFi-probe signal in the kicker-off condition, used to characterize non-stored transient circulation relative to the injected bunch width.

expected_output.experiment_description: The vertical distribution of the stored beam is measured to test whether the beam accumulated by the three-dimensional spiral injection method is governed by the intentionally applied weak-focusing field rather than by accidental trapping. The same 297 keV/c, 80 keV, 100 ns pulsed electron beam, 0.7 rad pitch-angle injection, 22 cm ultra-compact weak-focusing storage ring, Bz = 8.77 mT storage-plane solenoidal field, and 45 A, 140 ns kicker-pulse spiral-injection configuration are used. Four weak-focusing field configurations are generated by setting the main and auxiliary solenoid coil currents to (IMAIN, IAUX) = (8.70 A, 5.20 A), (8.82 A, 5.67 A), (9.20 A, 7.16 A), and (9.60 A, 8.72 A), with opposite current polarities in the actual magnet circuit. For each configuration, the radial magnetic-field component Br as a function of vertical coordinate Z is characterized in the storage region and used to determine the storable vertical range; finite-element calculations are performed with Opera for comparison, and Monte Carlo tracking includes the dominant injection-trajectory uncertainty. The stored-beam population is probed with the same vertically inserted plastic scintillating-fiber detector, 1 mm in diameter and 20 cm long, read out by a photomultiplier tube. A Z-scan is performed by inserting the probe from above in 5 mm steps; at each probe-tip position Z, measured from the storage midplane Z = 0 cm, a waveform averaged over 1000 injected shots is recorded. The measured dependent signal for the scan is the time-integrated SciFi-probe voltage ISignal = integral VSignal(t) dt, where VSignal(t) is the measured probe voltage and the integration window is t = 560 ns to 9000 ns after injection, beginning just after the end of the kicker pulse. The upper edge of the stored-beam distribution is defined as the probe-tip Z position where ISignal decreases to 5 percent of its maximum value for that field configuration. This spatially resolved scan covers the vertical storage aperture region accessible from above and uses the integrated signal to average over a wide range of vertical and radial betatron phases.

per_file.paper_title: Experimental characterization of the hierarchy of quantum correlations in top quark pairs

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept and measurement configuration: use proton-proton collisions recorded with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV to treat the spin-1/2 top quark and top antiquark in top-quark-pair production as a two-qubit quantum system. The analysis uses the published CMS doubly differential lepton+jets measurement of top-quark and antiquark polarization coefficients and spin-correlation coefficients in bins of the top-pair invariant mass m(ttbar) and the absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is defined in the ttbar center-of-mass frame with respect to the proton-beam direction. The lepton+jets topology consists of one W boson decaying leptonically and the other hadronically; the spin analyzers are the charged lepton and the down-type quark from the W decay. The spatial-geometric analogue for this collider measurement is the resolved two-dimensional phase-space scope: m(ttbar) bins [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV crossed with |cos(theta)| bins [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. The spin basis is the helicity basis, an event-dependent right-handed coordinate system in the ttbar rest frame with unit vectors (khat, nhat, rhat), where khat is the top-quark flight direction, rhat=(phat-cos(theta) khat)/sin(theta), nhat=rhat x khat, phat is the proton-beam direction, and the sign convention is nhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) nhat, rhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) rhat, khat -> khat. Because this basis changes orientation with event kinematics, the derived spin states correspond to the event-dependent, or fictitious, quantum-state construction used to characterize the hierarchy of quantum correlations. In each phase-space bin reconstruct the two-qubit spin density matrix rho_ttbar = (1/4)[I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j], where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the 3 by 3 spin-correlation matrix. Evaluate: top-quark discord D_t = S(rho_antitop) - S(rho_ttbar) + min_uhat[p_+ S(rho_top,+uhat)+p_- S(rho_top,-uhat)], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), uhat is the projective spin-measurement axis on the antitop, p_+ and p_- are the corresponding outcome probabilities, and rho_top,+uhat and rho_top,-uhat are the post-measurement top-quark states; the entanglement marker Delta_E from the Peres-Horodecki criterion as reported for the same reconstructed density matrices, with Delta_E greater than 1 defining the entangled region; the steering marker T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the integration over all unit-vector orientations and threshold 2*pi; the Bell-correlation marker B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C and threshold is 1 for CHSH Bell-correlated states; and the mixed-state quantum magic M2_tilde = -log2([1+sum_i(P_i^4+Pbar_i^4)+sum_ij C_ij^4]/[1+sum_i(P_i^2+Pbar_i^2)+sum_ij C_ij^2]). For each observable, use the Gaussian likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U_ij^{-1} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are the measured polarization and spin-correlation coefficients in the specified bin, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are the fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1]; central observable values are obtained at the likelihood minimum while holding the relevant observable definition fixed.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept and measurement configuration: use proton-proton collisions recorded with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV to treat the spin-1/2 top quark and top antiquark in top-quark-pair production as a two-qubit quantum system, and evaluate the hierarchy of quantum correlations in a fixed spin basis that corresponds to bona fide spin quantum states. The analysis uses the published CMS doubly differential lepton+jets measurement of top-quark and antiquark polarization coefficients and spin-correlation coefficients in bins of the top-pair invariant mass m(ttbar) and the absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is defined in the ttbar center-of-mass frame with respect to the proton-beam direction. The lepton+jets topology consists of one W boson decaying leptonically and the other hadronically; the spin analyzers are the charged lepton and the down-type quark from the W decay. The spatial-geometric analogue for this collider measurement is the resolved two-dimensional phase-space scope: m(ttbar) bins [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV crossed with |cos(theta)| bins [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. The spin basis is the beam basis, a fixed right-handed coordinate system in the ttbar rest frame with axes (xhat,yhat,zhat), where xhat points toward the center of the LHC ring, yhat is vertically upward, and zhat is along the proton beam axis phat. In each phase-space bin reconstruct the two-qubit spin density matrix rho_ttbar = (1/4)[I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j], where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the 3 by 3 spin-correlation matrix. Evaluate: top-quark discord D_t = S(rho_antitop) - S(rho_ttbar) + min_uhat[p_+ S(rho_top,+uhat)+p_- S(rho_top,-uhat)], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), uhat is the projective spin-measurement axis on the antitop, p_+ and p_- are the corresponding outcome probabilities, and rho_top,+uhat and rho_top,-uhat are the post-measurement top-quark states; the entanglement marker Delta_E from the Peres-Horodecki criterion as reported for the same reconstructed density matrices, with Delta_E greater than 1 defining the entangled region; the steering marker T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the integration over all unit-vector orientations and threshold 2*pi; the Bell-correlation marker B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C and threshold is 1 for CHSH Bell-correlated states; and the mixed-state quantum magic M2_tilde = -log2([1+sum_i(P_i^4+Pbar_i^4)+sum_ij C_ij^4]/[1+sum_i(P_i^2+Pbar_i^2)+sum_ij C_ij^2]). For each observable, use the Gaussian likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U_ij^{-1} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are the measured polarization and spin-correlation coefficients in the specified bin, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are the fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1]; central observable values are obtained at the likelihood minimum while holding the relevant observable definition fixed.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept and measurement configuration: use proton-proton collisions recorded with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV to treat the spin-1/2 top quark and top antiquark in top-quark-pair production as a two-qubit quantum system, and evaluate the hierarchy of quantum correlations in a fixed spin basis that corresponds to bona fide spin quantum states. The analysis uses the published CMS doubly differential lepton+jets measurement of top-quark and antiquark polarization coefficients and spin-correlation coefficients in bins of the top-pair invariant mass m(ttbar) and the absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is defined in the ttbar center-of-mass frame with respect to the proton-beam direction. The lepton+jets topology consists of one W boson decaying leptonically and the other hadronically; the spin analyzers are the charged lepton and the down-type quark from the W decay. The spatial-geometric analogue for this collider measurement is the resolved two-dimensional phase-space scope: m(ttbar) bins [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV crossed with |cos(theta)| bins [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. The spin basis is the beam basis, a fixed right-handed coordinate system in the ttbar rest frame with axes (xhat,yhat,zhat), where xhat points toward the center of the LHC ring, yhat is vertically upward, and zhat is along the proton beam axis phat. In each phase-space bin reconstruct the two-qubit spin density matrix rho_ttbar = (1/4)[I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j], where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the 3 by 3 spin-correlation matrix. Evaluate: top-quark discord D_t = S(rho_antitop) - S(rho_ttbar) + min_uhat[p_+ S(rho_top,+uhat)+p_- S(rho_top,-uhat)], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), uhat is the projective spin-measurement axis on the antitop, p_+ and p_- are the corresponding outcome probabilities, and rho_top,+uhat and rho_top,-uhat are the post-measurement top-quark states; the entanglement marker Delta_E from the Peres-Horodecki criterion as reported for the same reconstructed density matrices, with Delta_E greater than 1 defining the entangled region; the steering marker T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the integration over all unit-vector orientations and threshold 2*pi; the Bell-correlation marker B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C and threshold is 1 for CHSH Bell-correlated states; and the mixed-state quantum magic M2_tilde = -log2([1+sum_i(P_i^4+Pbar_i^4)+sum_ij C_ij^4]/[1+sum_i(P_i^2+Pbar_i^2)+sum_ij C_ij^2]). For each observable, use the Gaussian likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U_ij^{-1} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are the measured polarization and spin-correlation coefficients in the specified bin, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are the fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1]; central observable values are obtained at the likelihood minimum while holding the relevant observable definition fixed.

per_file.paper_title: Energy-resolved transport of ultracold atoms across the Anderson transition: theory and experiment

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: a three-dimensional, state-dependent optical speckle potential provides the disordered medium in which radio-frequency-selected ultracold 87Rb matter waves are tested for Anderson localization, diffusion, and critical transport. To characterize the disorder used for both the experiment and the ab initio simulations, generate or measure a blue-detuned laser speckle potential with strictly positive potential values. In the numerical implementation, use a Fourier-filtering construction of the speckle electric field on a regular rectangular grid covering a volume of (100 µm)^3, with grid spacings typically Δx = 0.7 µm and Δy = Δz = 0.3 µm. Model the experimental optical system as a λ = 780 nm laser beam propagating along x, linearly polarized in the y–z plane, incident on a diffusive lens with Gaussian beam waist w = 9.9 mm, truncated by a diaphragm of diameter D = 20.4 mm, and focused by a lens of focal length d = 15.2 mm. Set the disorder amplitude to VR/h = 416 Hz. Compute the potential V(r) = VR |E(r)|^2/I from the filtered random complex Gaussian field, and evaluate the normalized autocorrelation C(Δr) = δV(r)δV(r+Δr)/VR^2 with δV = V − VR. The spatial characterization compares two-dimensional cuts through the three-dimensional potential over the simulated 100 µm scale and autocorrelation line cuts along the longitudinal x direction and a transverse direction over displacement ranges sufficient to resolve the speckle-grain half-widths. Correlation lengths are defined as the autocorrelation half width at half maximum divided by 1.39156, and the geometric-mean correlation length σ defines Eσ = ℏ^2/(mσ^2). The goal is to determine the spatial correlation statistics and probability distribution of the disorder potential used for energy-resolved Anderson-transport measurements.

speckle_potential_distribution.description: The probability law of the positive blue-detuned speckle potential values.

longitudinal_correlation_length_um.description: The speckle correlation length along the elongated longitudinal x direction, using the stated half-width normalization convention.

transverse_correlation_length_um.description: The speckle correlation length in a transverse direction in the y–z plane, using the stated half-width normalization convention.

geometric_mean_correlation_length_um.description: The geometric-mean speckle correlation length over the three spatial directions.

correlation_energy_hz.description: The disorder correlation energy expressed as Eσ/h, where Eσ = ℏ^2/(mσ^2).

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: energy-resolved transport across the three-dimensional Anderson transition is enabled by transferring a small fraction of atoms from a disorder-insensitive hyperfine state into a disorder-sensitive state with a radio-frequency pulse whose detuning selects the target energy. Start with an ultracold 87Rb Bose gas in state |1⟩ = |F = 2, mF = 1⟩ in a nearly isotropic optical trap with trap frequencies approximately 2π × (35, 25, 11) Hz, temperature about 7 nK, chemical potential µin/h about 350 Hz, and Thomas–Fermi radii about (8, 12, 26) µm. The atom number is about 2 × 10^5, with a condensate fraction fc used in the energy-distribution model and a residual thermal fraction 1 − fc. Apply a bichromatic state-dependent optical speckle disorder of amplitude VR/h = 416 Hz, and use a weak-coupling radio-frequency pulse of duration trf ≃ 40 ms and Kaiser temporal envelope to transfer approximately 5% of atoms to |2⟩ = |F = 1, mF = −1⟩. The radio-frequency detuning δrf from the bare resonance sets Ef = ℏδrf. Immediately after transfer, switch off the optical trap and remove atoms left in |1⟩. For the formula result, E is the final atom energy in the disorder-sensitive state; Ef is the rf-selected target energy; fc is the condensate fraction; F(E − Ef) is the energy-filter intensity set by the rf pulse envelope; A(E,k=0) is the zero-momentum spectral function in the random potential; kB is Boltzmann’s constant; T is the initial cloud temperature; Θ is the Heaviside step function; and D(E;Ef) is normalized as the transferred-atom energy probability density. The goal is to determine the energy distribution produced by this rf-transfer preparation, including the contribution of the thermal component.

rf_filtered_rms_energy_width_hz.description: The root-mean-square energy width of the radio-frequency energy filter expressed as ΔE/h.

initial_condensate_fraction.description: The condensate fraction of the atomic cloud in the disorder-insensitive state used in the transferred-energy distribution model.

initial_thermal_fraction.description: The noncondensed thermal fraction of the atomic cloud in the disorder-insensitive state used in the transferred-energy distribution model.

transferred_energy_distribution.description: The modeled energy probability density of atoms transferred into the disorder-sensitive state, including Bose-condensed and thermal contributions.
transferred_energy_distribution.result: D(E;E_f)=f_c F(E-E_f)A(E,k=0)+(1-f_c)D_th(E;E_f), with D_th(E;E_f)=2(k_B T)^(-3/2)/sqrt(pi) * Theta(E-E_f)*sqrt(E-E_f)*exp[-(E-E_f)/(k_B T)]

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: after rf preparation of a narrow-energy matter wave in a three-dimensional disordered potential, the subsequent in-situ density evolution is used to identify localized, critical, and diffusive transport across the Anderson mobility edge. Prepare 87Rb atoms as a Bose-condensed cloud in |1⟩ = |F = 2, mF = 1⟩, transfer about 5% to |2⟩ = |F = 1, mF = −1⟩ using the 40 ms rf pulse in the state-dependent speckle potential of amplitude VR/h = 416 Hz, and choose target energies Ef/h = 166 Hz, 246 Hz, and 366 Hz. After transfer, set t = 0 by switching off the optical trap and removing atoms in |1⟩. Keep the atoms suspended against gravity by magnetic levitation; the residual confinement is shallow and lies in the horizontal x–y plane, while the analysis focuses on expansion along vertical z. Image the atoms in situ by fluorescence along x, giving a column density ncol(y,z,t) = ∫ dx nexp(r,t), then integrate over y to obtain n1d(z,t) = ∫ dy ncol(y,z,t). Record initial profiles immediately after transfer and subsequent profiles at evolution times including 1 s, 3 s, and 5 s. Analyze spatial profiles over the resolved z range shown in the data, approximately from −100 µm to +100 µm for the long-time comparison and about −80 µm to +80 µm for the time-series comparison, with each plotted point averaged over 6–9 independent experimental runs and error bars given as the standard error of the mean. Compare the profiles with the self-consistent-theory prediction using the experimentally measured initial n1d(z,0), an asymmetric pseudo-Voigt fit to that initial profile, and the rf-transfer energy distribution including the measured thermal fraction. The self-consistent-theory fit uses the central density n1d(0,t) over target energies near the transition and times up to 3 s to determine α0 and β, where α0 has units s^(−1/3), β has units µm s^(−1/3), and Ec is the mobility edge separating localized from diffusive dynamics.

experimental_mobility_edge_hz.description: The experimentally determined Anderson mobility-edge energy Ec/h used for the density-profile comparison.

sct_fit_alpha0_s_minus_1_3_experiment.description: The α0 parameter obtained by fitting the self-consistent localization theory to the experimental central-density dynamics.

sct_fit_beta_um_s_minus_1_3_experiment.description: The β parameter obtained by fitting the self-consistent localization theory to the experimental central-density dynamics.

transport_regime_Ef_166_hz_experiment.description: The transport regime assigned from the measured one-dimensional density-profile evolution at the specified target energy.

transport_regime_Ef_246_hz_experiment.description: The transport regime assigned from the measured one-dimensional density-profile evolution at the specified target energy.

transport_regime_Ef_366_hz_experiment.description: The transport regime assigned from the measured one-dimensional density-profile evolution at the specified target energy.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: a superconducting quantum annealing processor is operated as an analog-digital quantum computer by using independent “multicolor” annealing lines so that auxiliary source qubits implement programmable single-qubit state preparation, target qubits evolve under a time-independent analog Hamiltonian, and auxiliary detector qubits implement programmable-basis readout. The single-qubit characterization uses independent three-qubit source-target-detector systems on a 1178-qubit D-Wave Advantage2-type quantum annealing processor with six low-frequency annealing lines, each line controlling an anneal parameter s. For each source-target-detector triplet, all qubits start at s=0; the source qubit is forward-annealed to s=1 in a polarizing flux bias and the bias is then removed; the target qubit is brought to a fixed operating point with transverse splitting Delta/h=1.0 GHz and no programmed longitudinal field; the source is rapidly quenched back to s=0 to define the target initial state; after a variable free-evolution time t under H0=-(Delta/2) sigma_z, the detector qubit is rapidly annealed to s=1 and its flux state is measured. Source and detector static flux biases are independently swept from -200 microPhi0 to +200 microPhi0 to map the prepared Bloch vector n_s=(sin(theta_s)cos(phi_s), sin(theta_s)sin(phi_s), cos(theta_s)) and the detector measurement vector n_d=(sin(theta_d)cos(phi_d), sin(theta_d)sin(phi_d), cos(theta_d)). Magnetization data are taken as 1000-shot QPU calls for each t; short-time overlap between initialization and detection is excluded, and fits use the Larmor-precession/decoherence model over the stated fitting window. The fitted observable is <sigma_{n_d}>, where sigma_{n_d}=R_{theta_d,phi_d} sigma_z R^{-1}_{theta_d,phi_d}. The model used for extraction is <sigma_{n_d}>=cos(theta_d)[1-exp(-(t-t0)/T1)(1-cos(theta_s))]+sin(theta_d)sin(theta_s)cos[Delta(t-t0)/hbar+phi_s-phi_d]exp(-(t-t0)/T2), with T2=(1/(2T1)+1/T_phi)^(-1); t0 is the initialization time, T1 is the relaxation time, T_phi is the pure dephasing time, and hbar is the reduced Planck constant. The spatial/statistical scope is the median over 124 independent source-target-detector triplets distributed on the processor, after calibration of per-line delays, per-qubit anneal offsets, and per-qubit flux biases to align the degeneracy point and Larmor phase.

single_qubit_pure_dephasing_time_Tphi_ns.description: Median pure dephasing time extracted from the single-target-qubit arbitrary-basis Larmor-precession fits across the calibrated source-target-detector triplets.

source_and_detector_polar_angle_tuning.description: Whether the source and detector flux-bias controls allowed independent continuous tuning of the target preparation and readout polar angles over the Bloch sphere polar interval.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: the same multicolor analog-digital annealing protocol should remain usable when target-target couplings are left on during initialization and readout, so that two-qubit analog evolution can be measured in more than one basis. The experiment uses pairs of target qubits q1 and q2 on the 1178-qubit superconducting annealing processor, each target having a distinct source qubit and a distinct detector qubit controlled by separate annealing-line classes. All target qubits are operated at Delta/h=1.0 GHz with site detunings deltaDelta_i=0 and no programmed longitudinal fields. The two-target effective Hamiltonian in the weak-coupling rotating-wave regime is H_2Q=(J/4)(sigma_x1 sigma_x2+sigma_y1 sigma_y2), where J is the programmed exchange coupling energy. The protocol prepares product states using source-qubit pi/2 or pi pulses, evolves for variable time t over the plotted 0-30 ns window, and reads either sigma_x-basis or sigma_z-basis magnetizations using detector-qubit bias settings. Measurements include configurations with J/h=0, J/h=0.30 GHz, and J/h=0.15 GHz in the main characterization, with supplementary sigma_z-basis fits also varying J/h over 0.09, 0.15, 0.30, and 0.60 GHz. The relaxation of <sigma_z1 sigma_z2> and the dephasing of the oscillatory difference <sigma_z1>-<sigma_z2> are fit to an independent-noise two-qubit Lindblad model with identical per-qubit T1 and T_phi, using expressions such as <sigma_z1>=1-exp(-t/T1)[1+exp(-t/T_phi)cos(Jt/hbar)], <sigma_z2>=1-exp(-t/T1)[1-exp(-t/T_phi)cos(Jt/hbar)], and <sigma_z1 sigma_z2>=1-2exp(-t/T1). The quoted fitted medians are obtained from 62 different target-qubit pairs for the sigma_z-basis exchange condition with J/h=0.30 GHz.
