two_qubit_pure_dephasing_time_Tphi_ns.description: Median pure dephasing time extracted from the two-target-qubit spin-exchange oscillations using the open-system model.

two_qubit_total_dephasing_time_T2_ns.description: Total single-qubit coherence time derived from the fitted two-target-qubit relaxation and pure-dephasing parameters using T2=(1/(2T1)+1/T_phi)^(-1).

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: after source-qubit preparation and detector-qubit readout, a large chain of target qubits in a quantum annealer can be used as an analog simulator of coherent many-body dynamics; in the weak-coupling regime the target Hamiltonian is described by an effective XY model or, equivalently for the clean periodic chain, by a transverse-field Ising model whose single-excitation dispersion can be extracted from space-time-resolved magnetization. The experiment embeds a periodic one-dimensional chain of L=56 target qubits on the 1178-qubit processor, with each target coupled to a distinct source and detector qubit; four annealing-line color classes are assigned to target qubits and the remaining two to source and detector qubits. The target chain is programmed with uniform transverse splitting Delta/h=2.0 GHz, zero site detuning deltaDelta_i=0, nearest-neighbor periodic exchange coupling J/h=-0.60 GHz, and no longitudinal fields. A single target site is prepared in |+> by a source-qubit pi/2 operation while the rest of the chain is left in the target ground-state basis, the chain evolves for variable detector delay corresponding to normalized time |J|t/hbar spanning the plotted range, and all targets are read out in the sigma_x basis by detector qubits. The spatial scope is the full 56-site periodic ring; magnetization maps are averaged over all possible locations of the initially excited qubit and over the chain’s site-order-reversal symmetry, with each time/location measurement obtained from QPU shot averages. A two-dimensional Fourier transform over target-site index and evolution time is used to extract the magnetization spectral ridge. In the formula result, k is the quasimomentum in the first Brillouin zone [-pi,pi], Delta is the target transverse energy splitting, J is the nearest-neighbor exchange energy, E(k) is the positive or negative single-particle excitation energy, h is Planck’s constant, and hbar=h/(2pi).

sigma_x_chain_dispersion_relation_energy.description: Empirical single-paramagnon dispersion relation extracted from the space-time Fourier transform of the sigma_x magnetization in the clean periodic chain.

coherent_propagation_normalized_time_low.description: Lower-bound normalized evolution time over which coherent chain propagation is inferred under the clean-chain analog-digital protocol.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: the multicolor analog-digital protocol on a quantum annealer should measure a different dynamical correlator when the same clean target-chain analog evolution is initialized and read out in the energy basis rather than the transverse basis, allowing extraction of the energy-difference spectral structure of a periodic spin chain. The experiment embeds a periodic one-dimensional chain of L=124 target qubits on the 1178-qubit processor, with each target having a distinct source and detector qubit. Four annealing-line color classes control the target chain and two separate line classes control source and detector qubits. A single target site is prepared in |1> by a source-qubit pi pulse, the target chain evolves under the fixed clean-chain Hamiltonian for detector delays spanning the plotted normalized-time range |J|t/hbar, and all targets are measured in the sigma_z basis using detector-qubit readout. The spatial scope is the complete 124-site periodic ring; magnetization-derived excitation probabilities are averaged over all initially excited locations and over the chain’s bracelet symmetry, with QPU shot averaging for each time point. sigma_z_chain_fourier_peak_frequency_Hz.description: Empirical Fourier-transform peak frequency of the excitation-probability dynamics for the clean periodic chain measured in the sigma_z basis.

coherent_propagation_distance_qubits_low.description: Lower-bound propagation distance in lattice sites inferred for the clean-chain sigma_z excitation dynamics before loss of coherent propagation.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: the analog-digital quantum annealing protocol can intentionally program site-dependent target-qubit detunings in an effective XY chain and use arbitrary-basis initialization/readout to probe disorder-induced Anderson localization through the persistence of a spin-density-wave imbalance. The experiment uses a periodic one-dimensional chain of L=124 target qubits on the 1178-qubit processor, with each target assigned a distinct source and detector qubit. The clean target parameters are transverse splitting Delta/h=2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor exchange coupling J/h=0.20 GHz, and no programmed longitudinal field. Odd-indexed target qubits are prepared in |1> by source-qubit pi pulses to create the staggered initial configuration |1010...>, while even-indexed target qubits are left unexcited; all targets are then evolved under a fixed disordered chain Hamiltonian and measured in the sigma_z basis. Disorder is applied by programming per-qubit anneal offsets that implement detunings deltaDelta_i drawn uniformly from [-J W/2, J W/2], where W is the dimensionless disorder strength; unwanted coupling changes due to the same anneal offsets are compensated by reprogramming Jij values. The measured disorder strengths include W=0, 2, 4, and 8 for time traces over normalized time Jt/hbar spanning the plotted window, with QPU data averaged over 20 independent disorder realizations. The imbalance is computed from excitation probabilities as I(t)=[p_odd(t)-p_even(t)]/[p_odd(t)+p_even(t)], where p_odd=(1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2}[1-<sigma_z_{2i-1}>] and p_even=(1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2}[1-<sigma_z_{2i}>]. The long-time summary quantity I_tilde is the QPU imbalance averaged over normalized times Jt/hbar from 6*pi to 8*pi, and its small-W dependence is fit to a quadratic scaling form.

per_file.paper_title: Strong-field ionization of atoms with bright squeezed vacuum light

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: xenon strong-field ionization driven by BSV tests whether a nonclassical, zero-mean, strongly fluctuating optical field suppresses phase-sensitive above-threshold-ionization structures while preserving dynamically correlated photoelectron-holography pathways. BSV pulses generated by type-I degenerate SPDC near 1600 nm are focused by a 75 mm focal-length concave mirror into a pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet inside a COLTRIMS reaction microscope held at 5×10^-11 mbar. The xenon backing pressure is 0.7 atm, chosen to provide ionization yield while avoiding space-charge effects. Four BSV average pulse-energy conditions are used: 3.3, 5.0, 8.3, and 10 µJ, corresponding to average peak intensities of 0.53×10^14, 0.80×10^14, 1.33×10^14, and 1.60×10^14 W/cm^2. The BSV photon statistics are the characterized super-Poissonian distributions for these energy conditions. Electrons from the xenon target are extracted and guided by calibrated electric and magnetic fields to a microchannel-plate detector with a delay-line detector, giving time- and position-resolved single-electron detection. Millions of events are accumulated for each optical condition to reconstruct three-dimensional electron momenta. The reported momentum-distribution scope includes two-dimensional projections in p_x versus p_z over approximately p_x = -0.4 to 0.4 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u., and cylindrical projections p_r = sqrt(p_x^2+p_y^2) versus p_z over approximately p_r = 0 to 1 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u. The measurement targets interference features associated with direct, indirect, and forward-scattered subcycle electron trajectories in the focal-volume overlap of the gas jet and BSV beam; no spatially resolved target-volume map is reported.

bsv_driven_ati_peak_visibility.description: The visibility category of above-threshold-ionization peak/ring features in xenon PMDs under BSV driving across the measured pulse-energy conditions.

bsv_driven_spider_holographic_fringe_det.description: Whether spider-like photoelectron-holography fringes associated with indirect and forward-scattered electron trajectory interference are detected in the BSV-driven xenon PMDs across the measured conditions.

bsv_driven_non_spider_interference_visib.description: The visibility category of competing non-spider photoelectron interference structures in xenon PMDs under BSV driving.

bsv_driven_dominant_surviving_interferen.description: The trajectory-pair channel identified from the measured BSV-driven PMD morphology as the surviving holographic interference contribution.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: a coherent-state reference at the same mid-infrared wavelength provides the classical-field baseline for determining which xenon photoelectron-interference features are selectively filtered by BSV quantum fluctuations. In the COLTRIMS apparatus, the BSV beam is replaced by coherent-state mid-infrared pulses at 1600 nm generated by an optical parametric amplifier pumped by the same Ti:sapphire laser system. The coherent-state output is routed through the same optical path and focused into the same pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet with the same 75 mm focal-length concave mirror and target geometry used for BSV measurements. The chamber pressure is 5×10^-11 mbar, and the xenon backing pressure is 0.7 atm. The coherent-state peak intensity condition is 1.0×10^14 W/cm^2. Electrons are extracted and guided with calibrated electric and magnetic fields to an MCP plus delay-line detector for time- and position-resolved single-event measurement, with millions of events accumulated to reconstruct three-dimensional momenta. The reported reference PMD is plotted as p_r = sqrt(p_x^2+p_y^2) versus p_z over approximately p_r = 0 to 1 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u. report_experiments.experiment_description: Central concept: xenon strong-field ionization driven by BSV tests whether a nonclassical, zero-mean, strongly fluctuating optical field suppresses phase-sensitive above-threshold-ionization structures while preserving dynamically correlated photoelectron-holography pathways. BSV pulses generated by type-I degenerate SPDC near 1600 nm are focused by a 75 mm focal-length concave mirror into a pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet inside a COLTRIMS reaction microscope held at 5×10^-11 mbar. The xenon backing pressure is 0.7 atm, chosen to provide ionization yield while avoiding space-charge effects. Four BSV average pulse-energy conditions are used: 3.3, 5.0, 8.3, and 10 µJ, corresponding to average peak intensities of 0.53×10^14, 0.80×10^14, 1.33×10^14, and 1.60×10^14 W/cm^2. The BSV photon statistics are the characterized super-Poissonian distributions for these energy conditions. Electrons from the xenon target are extracted and guided by calibrated electric and magnetic fields to a microchannel-plate detector with a delay-line detector, giving time- and position-resolved single-electron detection. Millions of events are accumulated for each optical condition to reconstruct three-dimensional electron momenta. The reported momentum-distribution scope includes two-dimensional projections in p_x versus p_z over approximately p_x = -0.4 to 0.4 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u., and cylindrical projections p_r = sqrt(p_x^2+p_y^2) versus p_z over approximately p_r = 0 to 1 a.u. and p_z = -0.6 to 0.6 a.u. The measurement targets interference features associated with direct, indirect, and forward-scattered subcycle electron trajectories in the focal-volume overlap of the gas jet and BSV beam; no spatially resolved target-volume map is reported.

per_file.paper_title: Attosecond quantum spectroscopy with entangled photon pairs

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) generated by high-gain spontaneous parametric down-conversion is used as a quantum-light driver for high-harmonic generation, so the source must be characterized in photon statistics and spectral Schmidt-mode content before using it for attosecond quantum spectroscopy. A commercial femtosecond Yb:YAG fiber laser supplies near-infrared pump pulses at 1030 nm, 2 mJ pulse energy, 140 fs duration, and tunable repetition rate from 1 Hz to 10 kHz. A reduced-diameter portion of the pump is sent through two tandem type-I BBO crystals, each 3 mm thick, separated by approximately 40 cm to favor the lowest-divergence spatial mode. The SPDC output is spectrally filtered by a band-pass filter centered at 2050 nm with 100 nm FWHM to target the degenerate Schmidt mode. The single-pulse spectrum of the filtered quantum light is recorded with an AvaSpec-NIR256-2.5-HSC-EVO near-infrared spectrometer. More than 10000 single-shot spectra I(lambda) are analyzed by constructing the intensity covariance Cov(lambda,lambda') = <I(lambda)I(lambda')> - <I(lambda)><I(lambda')>, normalizing it to C(lambda,lambda') = Cov(lambda,lambda') / integral integral Cov(lambda,lambda') dlambda dlambda', and applying singular-value decomposition to extract orthonormal spectral Schmidt modes u_m(lambda) and mode weights lambda_m. Photon-number statistics are evaluated shot by shot; the time-domain zero-delay second-order correlation is defined here as g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the photon number per pulse in the measured filtered BSV mode. The optical path and measurement target the full collected SPDC beam after filtering rather than a selected spatial subregion; the spectral scope covers the near-infrared SPDC band around 1.8-2.3 micrometers, with spectral homogeneity assessed through the Schmidt-mode decomposition of the >10000-shot covariance matrix.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: high-harmonic generation in a solid is driven by a spectrally filtered degenerate-mode BSV field to test whether quantum photon-number fluctuations of the infrared driver are transferred to ultraviolet harmonics and whether the harmonic photon statistics can diagnose microscopic intraband-versus-interband emission channels. The quantum-light source is produced by high-gain type-I SPDC in two tandem 3 mm BBO crystals pumped at 1030 nm by 140 fs Yb:YAG pulses, with the SPDC output filtered by a 2050 nm, 100 nm FWHM band-pass filter. The filtered BSV driver is focused by an off-axis parabolic mirror of focal length 25.4 mm into the active region of a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal. The driver polarization is aligned along the crystal Gamma-Z axis. The driving intensity is set in the strong-field, nonperturbative solid-state HHG regime and approaches 1.2 TW/cm2 for the main single-mode measurement. Harmonics emitted from the illuminated through-thickness interaction volume are collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror and spectrally resolved with a Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer equipped with a PIX-100B high-efficiency detector. The measurement records single-pulse-resolved harmonic spectra, and photon-number distributions are evaluated separately for individual harmonic orders in the 2nd through 10th order range. For each harmonic order, N denotes the photon number in the spectral peak assigned to that harmonic order, and the reported photon bunching metric is g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2. The spectral-geometric scope is the collected emission from the focused spot in the 200 micrometer LN crystal, with harmonic coverage spanning the 2nd-10th orders of the approximately 2060 nm driver; comparison to the lithium niobate field-free bandgap of 3.3 eV provides the physical context for below-gap and above-gap harmonic channels.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: the proposed attosecond quantum-spectroscopy observable is the harmonic-order dependence of g2_tau0, so the experiment tests whether the same increase-then-decrease photon-bunching pattern persists when the filtered BSV driving intensity is changed. The BSV source is produced by the same 1030 nm, 140 fs Yb:YAG-pumped tandem type-I BBO SPDC geometry with two 3 mm BBO crystals separated by approximately 40 cm and with a 2050 nm, 100 nm FWHM band-pass filter selecting the degenerate spectral mode. The filtered BSV is focused by an f = 25.4 mm off-axis parabolic mirror into a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal, with polarization along the Gamma-Z axis. Harmonic emission from the focused interaction region is collected by a second off-axis parabolic mirror and recorded shot by shot with a Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer and PIX-100B detector. The independent variable is harmonic order over the measured 2nd-10th range, and the fixed comparison driving intensities are 0.57 TW/cm2 and 0.98 TW/cm2. For each harmonic order and intensity, the photon-number statistic is computed from the single-shot distribution using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the photon number in the corresponding harmonic spectral peak. The spatial scope is the collected output from the same focused spot geometry through the 200 micrometer LN crystal for both intensities, enabling comparison of order-dependent photon statistics under otherwise matched material orientation and detection conditions.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: without spectral filtering, the same high-gain SPDC source is intended to supply a low-dimensional multimode BSV containing non-degenerate Schmidt modes, i.e. bright entangled photon-pair components, whose wavelength-resolved correlations can be mapped through high-harmonic generation. The source uses near-infrared 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs pulses from the Yb:YAG laser at a tunable 1 Hz-10 kHz repetition rate, with a reduced-diameter beam sent into two 3 mm thick type-I BBO crystals in tandem and separated by approximately 40 cm to select the first spatial mode. No band-pass filter is placed after SPDC, so the collected near-infrared output contains the accessible lower-order spectral Schmidt modes of the generated BSV. The full collected SPDC beam is characterized with an AvaSpec-NIR256-2.5-HSC-EVO near-infrared spectrometer over the approximately 1800-2300 nm spectral interval. More than 10000 single-shot spectra are used for Schmidt-mode decomposition through the covariance matrix Cov(lambda,lambda'), its normalized form C(lambda,lambda'), and singular-value decomposition of the square-root matrix to obtain spectral modes and relative weights. Photon-number statistics are measured shot by shot over the collected multimode field, with g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2. Wavelength-resolved intensity correlations are computed as g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>), where N(lambda) is the photon number in a spectral bin centered at wavelength lambda. The normalized correlation parameter is Gamma(lambda,lambda') = [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda)g2(lambda')], with g2(lambda) defined as g2(lambda,lambda). The correlation maps target diagonal autocorrelation features and off-diagonal inter-wavelength co-fluctuations across the measured near-infrared BSV spectral band.

unfiltered_multimode_bsv_average_pulse_e.description: The measured average single-pulse energy reached by the unfiltered multimode BSV source under the stated operating constraints.

unfiltered_multimode_bsv_time_domain_g2_.description: The measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the unfiltered multimode BSV field using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

unfiltered_bsv_off_diagonal_spectral_cor.description: Whether the wavelength-resolved g2(lambda,lambda') and Gamma(lambda,lambda') maps contain off-diagonal inter-wavelength correlation features beyond the diagonal autocorrelation ridge.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: the non-degenerate bright entangled photon-pair components in the unfiltered BSV driver are used to test whether quantum-induced spectral correlations survive the strongly nonlinear up-conversion process into harmonic light. The unfiltered BSV driver is generated by high-gain type-I SPDC in two tandem 3 mm BBO crystals pumped by 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs Yb:YAG pulses, with approximately 40 cm crystal spacing and no spectral band-pass filter after SPDC. The resulting multimode quantum light is focused by an f = 25.4 mm off-axis parabolic mirror into a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal, with the driver polarization aligned along the Gamma-Z axis. The emitted harmonics from the focused through-thickness interaction region are collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror, dispersed by the Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer, and recorded shot by shot with a PIX-100B detector. The third-order harmonic is analyzed over the approximately 600-750 nm wavelength interval. Single-shot spectra are used both to compare total averaged third-harmonic spectra with subsets of pulses selected by their spectral structure and to compute wavelength-resolved correlations. The measured correlation functions are g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>) and Gamma(lambda,lambda') = [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda)g2(lambda')], where g2(lambda)=g2(lambda,lambda) and N(lambda) is the photon number in a third-harmonic wavelength bin. The analysis targets diagonal autocorrelation and off-diagonal lobes aligned with harmonic wavelengths associated with the non-degenerate Schmidt-mode sidebands, without using absolute intensity as the correlation metric.

third_harmonic_off_diagonal_g2_correlati.description: Whether the measured third-harmonic g2(lambda,lambda') map contains off-diagonal wavelength-correlation lobes beyond the diagonal autocorrelation ridge.

third_harmonic_off_diagonal_gamma_correl.description: Whether the measured third-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map contains off-diagonal wavelength-correlation lobes beyond the diagonal autocorrelation ridge.

bep_contribution_detected_in_third_harmo.description: Whether the third-harmonic spectral-correlation measurements detect a contribution associated with the non-degenerate bright entangled photon-pair components of the driver.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: the multimode BSV/BEP-driven HHG experiment is extended across harmonic orders to determine the harmonic-order range over which non-degenerate-pair-induced wavelength correlations remain spectrally resolvable after up-conversion. The second-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map is evaluated over approximately 950-1100 nm, and the fourth-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map is evaluated over approximately 450-550 nm. Gamma(lambda,lambda') is defined as [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda)g2(lambda')], with g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>) and g2(lambda)=g2(lambda,lambda). The spatial and spectral scope is the collected emission from the same LN focus, with maps inspected for off-diagonal inter-wavelength correlation structures as the indicator of BEP-related harmonic contributions.

The analysis targets diagonal autocorrelation and off-diagonal lobes aligned with harmonic wavelengths associated with the non-degenerate Schmidt-mode sidebands, without using absolute intensity as the correlation metric.

per_file.paper_title: Observation of feedback-directed quantum dynamics in large-scale quantum processors

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: feedback-directed quantum dynamics in random superconducting-qubit circuits, where spatially structured mid-circuit measurements are promoted from passive readout to real-time classical control signals. The experiment compares whether measurement alone or measurement-conditioned feedback creates directional information flow in an otherwise statistically symmetric random circuit, distinct from non-Hermitian skin-effect implementations with built-in asymmetric couplers. The hardware platform is the IBM Quantum superconducting processor “marrakesh” using native single-qubit RX rotations and CZ gates on a 1D chain of L = 20 qubits. Each circuit layer consists of a random scrambling unitary Urand built from alternating even- and odd-bond nearest-neighbor CZ gates plus independent random RX rotations RX_j(theta_j), with theta_j sampled in the strong-scrambling regime used in the main text. The initial computational-basis state contains six occupied qubits localized near the center of the 20-qubit chain. The layer index i is swept from 1 to 10. Four architectures are executed and compared over 10 independent random circuit realizations: (1) a purely unitary random circuit Uunitary(i) = [Urand]^i; (2) a random circuit with pure mid-circuit computational-basis measurements after each random layer, each qubit x measured with probability f(x) = (L - x)g using g = 0.01 and no feedback; (3) a conditional-X feedback circuit in which a measured outcome 0 triggers an X gate on the same qubit, with the same f(x) = (L - x)g and g = 0.01; and (4) a conditional-SWAP feedback circuit in which a measured outcome 0 on qubit x triggers a SWAP between x and x+1 with spatially uniform application probability pSWAP = 0.3. The measured local density is n_x = |0_x><0_x|, and the reported transport observable is the normalized center of mass Nc(i) = [sum_x x <n_x(i)>]/[sum_x <n_x(i)>], plotted in the paper in dimensionless chain-coordinate units. The spatial scope is the full 20-site chain; the local density profiles are resolved at every qubit and every circuit layer, and the center-of-mass values are averaged over the 10 random circuit realizations with standard-deviation error bars.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: scalability of feedback-directed non-unitary control in large random superconducting-qubit circuits. The experiment quantifies whether conditional-X feedback, driven by a spatially dependent mid-circuit measurement record, produces a center-of-mass displacement on a 100-qubit IBM Quantum chain, and compares it against two controls that lack feedback-directed dynamics. The hardware is the IBM Quantum processor “marrakesh,” with a 100-qubit low-noise 1D chain selected from the device layout. Each layer uses the same random scrambling block Urand composed of alternating nearest-neighbor CZ gates and random RX rotations, followed where applicable by a measurement layer. The initial state contains six occupied qubits. Two spatial placements are tested: six occupied qubits at the chain center and six occupied qubits near the right edge. The layer index i is swept from 1 to 10. The three circuit classes are: a purely unitary random circuit; a random circuit with position-dependent mid-circuit computational-basis measurements only; and a conditional-X feedback circuit in which qubit x is measured with probability f(x) = g(L - x), with g = 0.15/L, and outcome 0 triggers an X gate on that qubit. The measured density operator is n_x = |0_x><0_x|. The reported observable is the net center-of-mass shift delta_Nc(i) = L[Nc(i) - Nc(1)], where Nc(i) = [sum_x x <n_x(i)>]/[sum_x <n_x(i)>] and L = 100. The spatial scope is the full 100-qubit chain; the observable is computed from qubit-resolved final readout over all sites, and the plotted curves compare independent random circuit realizations averaged as in the main-text large-scale measurements.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept tested: a boundary-to-boundary polarization diagnostic for detecting feedback-directed transport in large random circuits when local bulk density profiles are noisy or spatially broad. The experiment runs large-scale IBM Quantum simulations on the superconducting processor “marrakesh” for L = 50, 80, and 100 qubit chains. Each chain is initialized with six occupied qubits at the center. The layer index i is swept from 1 to 10. Two circuit classes are compared: a purely unitary random circuit made from alternating nearest-neighbor CZ gates and random RX rotations, and a conditional-X feedback circuit with the same random scrambling layers followed by position-dependent mid-circuit computational-basis measurements. For the feedback circuit, qubit x is measured with probability f(x) = g(L - x), using the size-scaled gradient g = 0.18/L, and outcome 0 triggers an X gate on the measured qubit. The measured operator is n_x = |0_x><0_x|. The reported end-to-end polarization is Jc(i) = [<n_{L-1}(i)> - <n_0(i)>]/[sum_x <n_x(i)>], directly comparing the two ends of the full chain while normalizing by the total measured population. The spatial scope consists of the full chain for normalization and the two endpoint qubits for the numerator; each data set is averaged over 10 random circuit realizations with mean-deviation error bars and fitted solid curves.

per_file.paper_title: Polymer-free van der Waals assembly of 2D material heterostructures using muscovite crystals

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: use thin, crystalline, optically transparent muscovite mica as a polymer-free van der Waals transfer medium whose adhesion to 2D materials is tuned by temperature, enabling deterministic pick-up, stacking, and release without organic polymer contact. Atomic-force-microscopy-grade muscovite crystals are mechanically exfoliated with adhesive tape to produce few-hundred-nanometer-thick mica layers. For membrane stamps, a mica sheet is suspended over a 5–6 mm punched hole in Nitto ELP BT-50E-FR tape or several layers of Scotch Magic tape, transferred onto a rectangular PDMS block on a microscope glass slide, and tensioned by fixing the tape to the glass-slide sides. For cantilever stamps, a triangular mica sheet is cleaved from the tape edge, mounted on a metal support angled about 15 degrees on a microscope glass slide, and used as a freestanding transparent cantilever. Source mica and prepared stamps are stored under inert gas or in a dry vacuum desiccator; transfers are performed in argon glove-box or air conditions with ambient relative humidity kept below about 50% to limit water adsorption. For hBN/graphene/hBN assembly, a Si/SiO2 substrate containing an hBN flake is preheated to 50–90 °C, the mica stamp is brought into contact under an optical microscope by z-axis motion, the contact front is moved by z approach or by changing substrate temperature within ±10 °C, and full contact is made with the target flake before retraction. Subsequent 2D layers such as graphene are picked up using the already collected top hBN. For release, a target substrate carrying a bottom hBN flake is heated to 120–180 °C; the stack is brought into contact with the bottom hBN and the contact front is swept by temperature variation while leaving part of the bottom hBN uncovered by mica to test selective release of only the intended stack. The spatial scope is optical-microscope-guided flake-scale transfer over tens of micrometers in the active heterostructure region, using the mica membrane or cantilever as the only solid transfer support in place of PC/PPC polymer.

polymer_free_hbn_graphene_hbn_heterostru.description: Whether the mica membrane or cantilever protocol produced the intended hBN/graphene/hBN van der Waals heterostructure without a polymer transfer layer contacting the stack.

selective_stack_release_onto_bottom_hbn_.description: Whether the temperature-controlled mica protocol enabled release of the intended stack onto bottom hBN while retaining unwanted picked-up flakes on the mica stamp.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: evaluate whether the polymer-free mica cantilever transfer leaves atomically flat, clean hBN-encapsulated graphene interfaces without solvent cleaning or annealing. A single-layer graphene flake is fully encapsulated between top and bottom hBN using mica-cantilever-assisted assembly and the standard bottom-hBN release mechanism. The released stack is characterized as-is by contact-mode atomic force microscopy over the working area of the heterostructure, with the roughness extracted from a defined interior analysis window inside a several-micrometer AFM scan, away from visible flake edges and macroscopic contamination pockets. The measurement targets surface height variations of the top hBN over the active graphene-containing region after polymer-free release.

surface_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the mica-cantilever-assembled hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: test a polymer-free bottom-up assembly route in which a mica cantilever is incorporated as the supporting substrate by flipping the assembly and mechanically breaking off the cantilever, avoiding reliance on an additional bottom hBN release flake. A single-layer graphene flake is encapsulated in hBN on a graphite gate electrode using a mica cantilever; the cantilever is then flipped, broken off, and retained below the heterostructure as a mica layer. The sample is examined as-is by contact-mode AFM on the active hBN/graphene/hBN/graphite region, with roughness calculated from an interior analysis box inside a several-micrometer scan, away from flake boundaries and visible defects. The measurement targets whether the mica-supported heterostructure has an atomically flat exposed top surface after the polymer-free break-off release.

surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square topographic roughness of the mica-supported hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

surface_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the mica-supported hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether the mica membrane method can assemble a more complex multilayer van der Waals stack with clean interfaces and without post-transfer cleaning. A seven-layer heterostructure is assembled by mica-membrane-assisted transfer with the layer sequence hBN / twisted trilayer graphene / hBN / graphite / hBN; each graphene layer in the twisted trilayer graphene is intentionally misaligned by a high angle of about 20 degrees to decouple the graphene layers. The stack is released and characterized as-is without annealing, solvent immersion, or other cleaning. Contact-mode AFM is performed on the active multilayer region over an area exceeding 100 µm², and topographic roughness is extracted from an interior analysis window away from visible edges and bubbles. The measurement targets the surface flatness of the exposed top hBN above the multilayer graphene/graphite structure.

surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square topographic roughness of the mica-membrane-assembled hBN/twisted-trilayer-graphene/hBN/graphite/hBN stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

surface_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the mica-membrane-assembled hBN/twisted-trilayer-graphene/hBN/graphite/hBN stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: assess whether mica-assisted assembly can produce a clean, marginally twisted hBN/hBN moiré ferroelectric superlattice over a large flake-scale area, using the atomically flat mica surface and low-temperature release to preserve the twist configuration. A cracked hBN flake is used so that one piece is picked up with a mica membrane and released back onto another part of the same hBN flake at 50 °C, targeting marginal angular alignment. The resulting hBN/hBN stack is characterized by AFM height imaging and Kelvin probe force microscopy under scanning-probe conditions. The KPFM scans target nanoscale electrostatic-potential modulation associated with triangular ferroelectric moiré domains over the top hBN flake, including a large-area scan of the whole flake-scale region and a higher-resolution scan near a localized submicron interfacial bubble to test continuity and local deformation of the domain pattern.

moire_ferroelectric_superlattice_formed.description: Whether the marginally twisted hBN/hBN structure produced by mica-assisted assembly exhibited a ferroelectric moiré superlattice detectable by KPFM.

moire_domain_coverage_area_um2.description: The approximate area of the top hBN flake over which the ferroelectric moiré domains extended in KPFM characterization.

hbn_moire_superlattice_fabrication_yield.description: The approximate fabrication yield for hBN-based moiré superlattice structures using the mica-assisted protocol, as reported for this structure class.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: compare the mica-assisted polymer-free route with a conventional polycarbonate-based assembly for marginally twisted hBN/hBN moiré ferroelectrics, focusing on whether surface residues obstruct scanning-probe detection of the interfacial moiré potential. A marginally twisted hBN/hBN structure is assembled using a standard PC-assisted method, most of the PC is dissolved in dichloromethane for several hours, and the exposed surface is examined by KPFM before and after local contact-mode AFM mechanical cleaning. The scan covers both polymer-residue-covered regions and an AFM-cleaned region on the hBN/hBN stack, using the same type of ferroelectric moiré electrostatic contrast targeted in the mica-assisted hBN/hBN measurement.

moire_potential_screened_by_pc_residues.description: Whether polymer residues on the PC-assembled hBN/hBN stack screened the KPFM-detectable moiré ferroelectric potential in residue-covered regions.

moire_potential_detectable_after_afm_cle.description: Whether local contact-mode AFM cleaning enabled KPFM detection of the hBN/hBN moiré ferroelectric potential in the cleaned region.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: test whether a pre-characterized marginally aligned single-layer graphene/hBN moiré heterostructure can be picked up by a mica membrane while preserving the moiré wavelength and therefore the twist angle. A single-layer graphene on hBN stack is first assembled on SiO2/Si by a PC-based method and characterized by peak-force microscopy in a clean area between PC-residue traces. The heterostructure is then picked up using a mica membrane at 50 °C and re-characterized with the same AFM cantilever while supported by mica. Peak-force microscopy line profiles are compared along defined line cuts in the pre-pickup and post-pickup scans over a nanoscale moiré region, targeting the periodic adhesion or indentation modulation of the SLG/hBN moiré lattice rather than macroscopic flake morphology.

moire_wavelength_on_sio2_nm.description: The SLG/hBN moiré wavelength measured by peak-force microscopy before mica pickup while the heterostructure was on SiO2/Si.

moire_wavelength_on_mica_nm.description: The SLG/hBN moiré wavelength measured by peak-force microscopy after pickup onto the mica membrane.

moire_twist_angle_preserved_after_mica_p.description: Whether comparison of the SLG/hBN moiré wavelength before and after mica pickup indicated preservation of the twist angle.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: use polymer-free mica-membrane assembly to expose clean conductive twisted bilayer graphene surfaces for high-resolution conductive AFM, while deterministically setting sub-degree twist angles to tune the moiré period. Marginal-angle twisted bilayer graphene devices are assembled on thick graphite flakes by the mica-membrane method with nominal twist angles of about 0.8°, 0.3°, and 0.15°. Conductive AFM is performed in ambient air at room temperature with relative humidity below 56% using a Bruker Dimension Icon AFM, Nanoscope VII controller, PFTUNA module, and Pt-coated Si CONTV-PT tip of approximate radius 25 nm and spring constant about 0.2 N/m. Scanning is in contact mode at 0.5–1 Hz. The 0.8° scan uses 1 mV sample bias, -0.1 V deflection setpoint, and 256 × 256 pixels; the 0.3° scans use 0.4 mV bias, 0.02 V setpoint, and 512 × 512 or 256 × 256 pixels; the 0.15° scans use 7 mV bias, 0.08 V or 0.05 V setpoint, and 512 × 512 or 256 × 256 pixels. Current maps are first-order flattened. The scans span nanoscale fields of view from tens to hundreds of nanometers and target local tip-sample current variation associated with AA/AB/BA domains and domain walls, with the broader uniformity context assessed across up to micrometer-scale exposed TBG surface.

moire_period_for_0p8deg_tbg_nm.description: The moiré period measured by conductive AFM for the approximately 0.8° twisted bilayer graphene device.

aa_ab_ba_domain_structure_resolved_in_lo.description: Whether conductive AFM resolved AA, AB, and BA domain contrast and associated domain-wall structure in the lower-angle twisted bilayer graphene devices.

uniform_moire_area_um2.description: The approximate maximum area over which the exposed twisted bilayer graphene moiré superlattice was reported to remain uniform and clean for cAFM/STM-scale studies.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether mica-assisted assembly yields graphene Hall-bar electronic quality comparable to state-of-the-art clean van der Waals devices. A large-area hBN/single-layer-graphene/hBN heterostructure is assembled on SiO2/Si using the mica-assisted method and patterned into a Hall bar in a bubble-free region with approximate dimensions 20 µm by 14 µm. Low-temperature multiterminal non-local bend-resistance measurements are performed at T = 1.7 K. Charge-carrier density n is swept over approximately -1.5 × 10^12 to +1.0 × 10^12 cm^-2 and perpendicular magnetic field B over approximately -0.3 to +0.3 T in the non-local geometry, with current and voltage probes arranged across the Hall-bar width. The measurement targets ballistic transport signatures, magnetic electron focusing, and mobility as functions of carrier density in the active encapsulated graphene channel.

zero_field_negative_nonlocal_resistance_.description: Whether the hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene Hall bar exhibited negative non-local resistance at zero magnetic field in the bend-resistance geometry.

magnetic_electron_focusing_observed.description: Whether the non-local magnetotransport exhibited magnetic electron focusing oscillations.

high_density_electron_mobility_cm2_V_s.description: The electron mobility reached at high carrier density in the hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene Hall bar.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: test the mica-assisted method on a complex, high-angle twisted trilayer graphene heterostructure where low disorder and ballisticity are probed by low-field Landau quantization. A seven-layer hBN/twisted-trilayer-graphene/hBN/graphite/hBN heterostructure assembled by the mica membrane method, with the three graphene layers intentionally misaligned by high angles of about 20°, is fabricated into a Hall bar on SiO2/Si. Low-temperature non-local bend-resistance is measured as a function of total carrier density n and perpendicular magnetic field B, with an applied displacement field condition D = -0.5 V/nm for the non-local map. A double-gate resistance map is also measured at fixed B = 50 mT while sweeping carrier density over approximately -0.2 × 10^12 to +0.2 × 10^12 cm^-2 and displacement field over approximately -0.2 to +0.2 V/nm. The measurement targets ballistic bend resistance and the onset and multiplicity of Landau quantization from the top, middle, and bottom graphene layers.

zero_field_negative_bend_resistance_obse.description: Whether the high-angle twisted trilayer graphene Hall bar exhibited negative bend resistance at zero magnetic field.

landau_quantization_onset_mT.description: The magnetic-field scale at which Landau quantization became detectable in the high-angle twisted trilayer graphene Hall bar.

minimum_distinct_landau_levels_at_50mT.description: The reported lower bound on the number of distinct Landau levels observed in the double-gate map at 50 mT.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: evaluate whether a heterostructure assembled on a mica cantilever and released by flipping and breaking off the cantilever can function as a high-quality gated graphene Hall-bar device with mica retained as part of the substrate stack. An hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene heterostructure on a bottom graphite gate is assembled on a freestanding mica cantilever, then flipped and mechanically broken off so the mica remains below the stack. The device is patterned into a Hall bar; the bottom graphite is used as a bottom gate and Ti/Au is used as a top gate, with metal contacts routed over the several-hundred-nanometer-thick mica support. Longitudinal resistivity is measured versus gate voltage during ascending and descending gate sweeps at T = 300 K and again after cooling to T = 1.5 K. Mean free path is extracted at T = 1.5 K as a function of carrier density and compared with the Hall-bar width indicated by the device geometry. The measurement targets hysteresis, Dirac-peak asymmetry, and whether the electronic mean free path reaches the geometric limit.

room_temperature_gate_hysteresis_observe.description: Whether the mica-supported hBN-encapsulated graphene Hall bar exhibited gate-sweep hysteresis at room temperature.

large_dirac_peak_asymmetry_observed.description: Whether the mica-supported graphene Hall bar exhibited a large asymmetry of the Dirac peak between opposite gate-sweep directions.

mean_free_path_limited_by_hall_bar_width.description: Whether the extracted low-temperature electron mean free path was limited by the Hall-bar width.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: use solvent-free mica-assisted transfer to fabricate suspended 2D heterostructure membranes suitable for nanomechanics, avoiding liquid processing that can damage suspended devices. A single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure is assembled with the same mica-assisted transfer conditions used for supported stacks and suspended over a circular hole etched in a bottom hBN flake on SiO2, forming a membrane with diameter d = 3 µm. The membrane surface is inspected by peak-force microscopy over the suspended region to target surface continuity and cleanliness. Static force-deflection AFM is then performed at the center of the suspended membrane; force is swept up to approximately 800 nN while indentation is recorded up to approximately 50 nm. The force-deflection curve is fit to the standard continuum-mechanics model for a circular membrane, extracting Young's modulus E and pre-tension N0, where E is the in-plane elastic modulus of the suspended heterostructure membrane and N0 is the built-in membrane tension per unit length.

suspended_slg_hbn_membrane_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted procedure produced a suspended single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure membrane over the etched hBN cavity.

youngs_modulus_GPa.description: The Young's modulus extracted from continuum-mechanics fitting of the static AFM force-deflection curve of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane.

pre_tension_N_m.description: The membrane pre-tension per unit length extracted from continuum-mechanics fitting of the static AFM force-deflection curve of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: characterize the dynamic nanomechanical response of a solvent-free mica-transferred suspended single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure membrane. The same circular d = 3 µm SLG/hBN membrane suspended over an hBN cavity is mounted inside an Attocube attoDRY800 optical cryostat on an xy positioning stage and cooled to T = 4 K under high vacuum. A power-modulated blue diode laser with wavelength 450 nm actuates membrane motion, and a HeNe red laser with wavelength 633 nm reads out displacement interferometrically; both laser spots are about 1 µm and incident laser powers are below 1 µW. The response amplitude is processed by a vector network analyzer while sweeping drive frequency over the fundamental-mode resonance region around 23.4–24.2 MHz. The resonance spectrum is fit to a linear damped harmonic-oscillator model to extract the resonance frequency f0 and mechanical quality factor Q.

fundamental_resonance_frequency_MHz.description: The fundamental mechanical resonance frequency extracted from the damped harmonic-oscillator fit of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane response.

mechanical_quality_factor.description: The mechanical quality factor extracted from the damped harmonic-oscillator fit of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane response.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: extend mica-assisted solvent-free transfer to suspended moiré membranes, where substrate-free aligned graphene/hBN superlattices can be examined by scanning probe methods. An aligned single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure, with the hBN component being 1–2 layers, is fabricated by mica-assisted transfer and suspended over a pre-etched circular cavity in hBN with diameter d = 0.5 µm. Peak-force microscopy adhesion mapping is performed over the full suspended membrane area with nanoscale lateral resolution to target the periodic adhesion modulation of the SLG/hBN moiré lattice across the free-standing region, including assessment of whether the periodic pattern extends to the membrane boundary rather than being limited to a supported substrate region.

suspended_slg_hbn_moire_membrane_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted transfer produced a suspended aligned SLG/hBN moiré heterostructure membrane over the hBN cavity.

moire_pattern_spans_suspended_membrane.description: Whether the PFM adhesion map detected the SLG/hBN moiré pattern over the suspended membrane surface.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: test whether mica cantilevers can manipulate non-graphene van der Waals ferroelectrics without polymer residues, using folded 3R-MoS2 as a target structure relevant for mirror-twin-boundary ferroelectric interfaces. A large 3R-MoS2 flake is contacted by a mica cantilever; part of the flake is picked up, folded onto itself, and then delaminated and released by sliding the flake off the cantilever while moving parallel to the substrate surface. The resulting folded and unfolded 3R-MoS2 regions are characterized by AFM over interior areas of each region, away from the fold edge and macroscopic flake boundaries. The measurement targets the topographic roughness of the polymer-free folded interface and the adjacent original region.

folded_3r_mos2_structure_formed.description: Whether the mica-cantilever folding and sliding release procedure produced a folded 3R-MoS2 structure.

folded_region_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the folded 3R-MoS2 region measured by AFM.

unfolded_region_peak_to_peak_roughness_p.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the adjacent unfolded 3R-MoS2 region measured by AFM.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: demonstrate that mica-assisted polymer-free transfer can produce open, uncapped monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures with clean surfaces suitable for optical measurements. A monolayer MoS2 flake is transferred onto an hBN substrate using the mica-assisted procedure; for materials other than hBN, the mica may be mildly treated by UV/O3 at 60 °C for 12 min to improve adhesion. The uncapped MoS2/hBN stack is characterized in ambient air at room temperature. AFM height mapping is used to assess the top surface over the monolayer flake region, and photoluminescence spectroscopy is collected over the visible spectral window corresponding to wavelengths 550–750 nm, targeting the MoS2 excitonic emission from the transferred monolayer.

mos2_surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square surface roughness of the uncapped monolayer MoS2 on hBN measured by AFM.

room_temperature_pl_peak_energy_eV.description: The photoluminescence peak energy of the uncapped monolayer MoS2 on hBN measured in air at room temperature.

room_temperature_pl_fwhm_meV.description: The full width at half maximum of the room-temperature photoluminescence peak of the uncapped monolayer MoS2 on hBN.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: assess the broader material compatibility of the mica-assisted polymer-free transfer method beyond graphene and hBN, including exposed conductive layers and air-sensitive magnetic crystals. The same mica-assisted pick-up, stacking, and release strategy is applied to fabricate open single-layer graphene on hBN, hBN-encapsulated few-layer CrBr3, and few-layer FePS3 on hBN. Transfers are performed under dry or inert conditions compatible with mica adhesion control; for top materials with weaker adhesion than hBN, mild UV/O3 treatment of mica at 60 °C for 12 min may be used. Optical microscopy is used over tens-of-micrometers flake-scale areas to assess whether the intended target flakes remain continuous and positioned on the hBN supports or encapsulated between hBN layers, with special attention to the uncapped or air-sensitive active material regions.

uncapped_slg_on_hbn_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted method produced an uncapped single-layer graphene on hBN heterostructure.

hbn_encapsulated_few_layer_crbr3_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted method produced an hBN-encapsulated few-layer CrBr3 heterostructure.

few_layer_feps3_on_hbn_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted method produced a few-layer FePS3 on hBN heterostructure.

expected_output.experiment_description: Central concept: characterize environmental control of mica adhesion, which underlies the temperature-tunable polymer-free transfer mechanism. Adhesion forces between gold-plated mica cantilevers and representative surfaces including graphite, hBN, and SiO2 are measured by AFM force-deflection methods in ambient conditions while varying humidity and substrate temperature. High-humidity conditions are defined as relative humidity above about 60%, and low-humidity transfer-relevant conditions are compared while increasing the substrate temperature above room temperature up to the range in which the transfer protocol operates. The measurement targets the contact adhesion force between mica and the 2D-material or substrate surfaces, particularly the sensitivity of mica-hBN adhesion to adsorbed water and the reduction of adhesion at elevated temperature.
